Ubuhamya bwatanzwe n’abaturage bakora ubuhinzi bubungabunga ubutaka, baturutse mu bice bitandukanye by’igihugu, bugaragaza uburyo ubu buhinzi bwongera umusaruro ugereranyije n’ubuhinzi gakondo.

Iyi nama yabereye muri RICA kuri uyu wa Kane tariki ya 12 Ugushyingo 2026 yahuje abahinzi, abashakashatsi, inzego za Leta, abikorera n’abafatanyabikorwa mu iterambere ry’ubuhinzi bagera kuri 450, baganira ku buryo ubuhinzi bubungabunga ubutaka bwakwagurwa kugira ngo bugire uruhare mu kongera umusaruro no kubaka urwego rw’ibiribwa rurambye mu Rwanda.

Nyirambonimpa Saidat, ukomoka mu Karere ka Kirehe, akaba umwe mu bahinzi bigishijwe na Kaminuza ya RICA, yavuze ko mbere, ubwo yakoraga ubuhinzi gakondo, agahinga uko abyumva akoresheje isuka ya majagu, atabonaga umusaruro uhagije.

Ati: “Nahingaga ku buso bungana na Are eshanu, nkezaho ibiro 30 by’ibigori n’ibiro 20 by’ibishyimbo. Ariko nyuma yo kwigishwa gukora ubuhinzi bubungabunga ubutaka na RICA, kuri ubwo buso bwa are eshanu nsigaye neza ibiro bigera kuri 300 by’ibigori n’ibiro 280 by’ibishyimbo, iyo imihindagurikire y’ibihe yagenze neza.”

Nyirambonimpa yavuze ko mbere yahingaga agacukura ubutaka akagera kure cyane, ariko nyuma Kaminuza ya RICA ikamwigisha hamwe na bagenzi be ko umuntu aharura ubutaka, agacukura imyobo, agateramo imyaka hanyuma agasasira ubutaka.

Ati: “Iyo uhinze udacukuye ubutaka ukagera hasi cyane, usanga iyo imvura iguye amazi aguma mu butaka. Ibyo wasasiye imyaka bigahinduka ifumbire, kandi isuri ntishobora gutwara imyaka kuko ubutaka buba bukomeye.”

Nteziryayo Ignace, umunyamuryango w’Umuryango w’Abahinzi n’Aborozi mu Rwanda, na we yavuze ko gahunda yo guhinga habungabungwa ubutaka yamugiriye akamaro kuko yongereye umusaruro.

Gusa, Nteziryayo yasabye ko Leta yakongera ishoramari mu buhinzi bubungabunga ubutaka kugira ngo bukorwe ku kigero gishimishije.

Tuyizere Emmanuel na we wafashijwe na Kaminuza ya RICA, ibigisha ubuhinzi bubungabunga ubutaka, yavuze ko mbere uburyo bahingagamo bwangizaga ubutaka kubera ubumenyi buke bari bafite.

Yavuze ko bamaze kwigishwa guhinga neza, basasira ubutaka kandi ntibabucukure cyane, umusaruro wiyongereye. Yatanze urugero rw’uko ku buso bwa Are imwe bahasaruraga ibiro 25 by’ibigori, mu gihe ahahinze mu buryo bwo kubungabunga ubutaka, hakoreshwa ifumbire y’imborera n’ifumbire mvaruganda ndetse hagasasirwa ibyatsi, basaruye ibiro bisaga 70.

Umuyobozi wa Kaminuza ya RICA, Momar Dieng, yagaragaje ko iyo nama ari umwanya ukomeye wo guhuza inzego zitandukanye hagamijwe gushakira hamwe ibisubizo byafasha guteza imbere ubuhinzi burambye mu Rwanda.

Yavuze ko urwego rw’ubuhinzi rugihura n’imbogamizi zirimo kwangirika kw’ubutaka, isuri, imihindagurikire y’ikirere.

Ati: “Nk’uko bigaragazwa na Raporo y’u Rwanda igaragaza ingamba n’intego igihugu cyihaye mu guhangana n’imihindagurikire y’ikirere (NDC 3.0) yo mu 2025, ubutaka burenga hegitari miliyoni imwe buri mu byago bikomeye byo gutwarwa n’isuri, aho buri mwaka kuri hegitari imwe hatakara impuzandengo ya toni 25 z’ubutaka bwo hejuru. Ibyo bigaragaza ubukana bw’ikibazo cy’isuri n’ingaruka iteza ku musaruro w’ubuhinzi.”

Yakomeje avuga ko ubuhinzi bubungabunga ubutaka ari imwe mu nzira zafasha guhangana n’izo mbogamizi, binyuze mu mahame atatu y’ingenzi arimo kudahungabanya ubutaka cyane babucukura mu gihe cyo kubuhinga, kubusigasira bugahora butwikiriwe no guhinduranya ibihingwa.

Yashimangiye ko hakenewe kuva mu mishinga y’igerageza n’ibikorwa bikorerwa ahantu hihariye, ubu buhinzi bugashyirwa mu bikorwa ku rwego rwagutse binyuze muri gahunda na politiki by’igihugu, ishoramari, ubushakashatsi n’amahugurwa ahabwa abahinzi.

Dr. Olivier Kamana, Umunyamabanga wa Leta muri Minisiteri y’Ubuhinzi n’Ubworozi (MINAGRI), yavuze ko ubuhinzi bubungabunga ubutaka ari imwe mu nzira z’ingenzi u Rwanda rukwiye kwifashisha mu kongera umusaruro w’ibiribwa no guhangana n’ingaruka z’imihindagurikire y’ikirere.

Yasabye inzego za Leta, abafatanyabikorwa mu iterambere, ibigo by’imari n’abikorera gukorera hamwe mu gukemura izo mbogamizi, binyuze mu bushakashatsi bujyanye n’ibikenewe mu Rwanda, amahugurwa n’ubujyanama bihoraho bihabwa abahinzi.

Yagaragaje kandi ko urubyiruko rukwiye guhabwa amahirwe yo kugira uruhare muri ubu buhinzi binyuze mu ikoranabuhanga, gukoresha imashini n’ibikorwa by’ubucuruzi bishingiye ku buhinzi.

Dr. Olivier Kamana yashimangiye ko umusaruro w’iyi gahunda utazapimirwa gusa ku nama zabaye cyangwa abantu bahuguwe, ahubwo uzagaragarira mu mubare w’abahinzi bazitabira ubu buhinzi, mu buryo bwo kubungabunga ubutaka no mu musaruro uzava mu buhinzi burambye.

MN202611_khj1k0by0u.t:
The Tartan Army made a big impression on the city of Boston during the World Cup

BBC Scotland has learned that the SFA is in active discussions aimed at a biennial friendly match being held in Boston.

Scotland played two World Cup matches in the US city during the summer and now the governing body and the state of Massachusetts are in talks aimed at building the bonds made between locals and the Tartan Army, through football.

More discussions are due to take place between the SFA and a delegation of state senators ahead of Scotland's Nations League match against North Macedonia at Hampden on Friday.

It has not yet been decided who will play in the game but BBC Scotland understands it will involve the Scoland national team.

US state senator Paul Feeney has been in the UK this week for talks around energy, but wanted to visit Scotland to build on the bonds made between the Tartan Army and those who partied with them for two weeks in June.

The state of Massachusetts has also passed a bill aimed at strengthening ties with Scotland after an estimated 25,000 fans partied in Boston and surrounding areas.

"We felt that this summer was more than just a football match, more than just, you know, 90 minutes at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough," Feeney said.

"It was a couple of weeks of these relationships being held, and you don't see that often. And I'm glad we got to experience it. And, frankly, we don't want that to end."

He added: "One of the things that we've been active on in Massachusetts today is to kind of take the lessons that we've learned, put together the best practices, and say, ok, we understand that we can't have a World Cup every year, but where we have such a strong connection with people in Scotland, could we do some sort of invitational tournament?

"To have that cultural exchange to kind of prop up economic development, and more than that, just to come together, have a few drinks, and enjoy each other's company."

Scotland fans placed cones on several Boston statues during their time in the city

Feeney said the Massachusetts Senate voted unanimously to support the concept.

"We're trying to work that through the legislature, get it to the finish," he said.

Talks aimed at organising a regular fixture are at an early stage but the SFA is already in advanced negotiations with businesses in Massachusetts about investment in the Scottish game.

"The Tartan Army invaded Massachusetts and I have to say they lit a spark that set off fireworks," Massachusetts Senate president Karen Spilka told BBC Scotland.

"They were sorely missed by so many people when they left.

"I think that by making the effort to come here and meet people and talk about tourism and economic development, we can start talking about things like Tartan Day and maybe having other events going on."

Yabigarutseho ku wa 12 Ugushyingo 2026, mu nama nyunguranabitekerezo yo ku rwego rwo hejuru ku buhinzi buhangana n’imihindagurikire y’ibihe yabereye muri Antalya muri Turikiya.

Minisitiri w’Intebe yavuze ko imihindagurikire y’ibihe ari ikibazo abahinzi b’u Rwanda bahura na cyo mu buzima bwa buri munsi, cyane cyane iyo imvura ibaye nke cyangwa ikagwa ari nyinshi mu gihe gito, bikangiza imyaka, bigahungabanya umusaruro n’ubukungu bw’ingo.

Yagize ati: “Iyo imvura itaguye cyangwa ikagwa ari nyinshi kandi mu gihe gito, abahinzi bacu ni bo babanza kubyiyumvamo: ku misozi bahingaho, mu bubiko bw’imyaka ndetse no mu ngengo y’imari y’ingo zabo.”

Yavuze ko ubuhinzi butunga ingo zose mu Rwanda kandi bukaba isoko y’imibereho y’imiryango myinshi yo mu cyaro. Ni yo mpamvu ishoramari muri uru rwego rigomba gushingira ku buryo burinda umusaruro n’abahinzi ingaruka z’imihindagurikire y’ibihe.

Yashimangiye ko intego u Rwanda rwihaye yo kugera ku rwego rw’ibihugu bifite ubukungu bwo ku rwego rwo hejuru bitarenze mu 2050, nk'uko biteganywa muri Vision 2050, igomba gushingira ku iterambere rirambye kandi rishobora guhangana n’ihindagurika ry’ibihe.

Mu myaka isaga icumi ishize, u Rwanda rwashyizeho ingamba n’inzego zo gushyigikira iki cyerekezo, zirimo Ingamba zo Kwihutisha Iterambere Rishingiye ku Bukungu Buzigama Ibidukikije no Guhangana n’Imihindagurikire y’Ibihe, Ingamba zo Gutera Inkunga Ibikorwa by’Ikirere n’Ubuzima Kamere, Politiki y’Igihugu y’Ishoramari n’Ikigega cy’u Rwanda cy’Ibidukikije (Rwanda Green Fund).

Izi gahunda zahurijwe muri gahunda yiswe Climate and Development Country Platform, igamije guhuza ibyihutirwa mu iterambere, imishinga ikeneye ishoramari n’ubufatanye n’abafatanyabikorwa.

Atanga urugero rw’ibikorwa byamaze gukorwa, Minisitiri w’Intebe yagarutse ku mushinga wa Green Gicumbi, ugamije kongerera ubushobozi bwo guhangana n’imihindagurikire y’ibihe, ykaba waragize inyungu zitaziguye ku baturage bagera ku 249.000 bo mu Karere ka Gicumbi.

Uyu mushinga wafashije abaturage gukora amaterasi y’indinganire, kurinda amasoko y’amazi no kwimura imiryango yari ituye ahantu hashobora kwibasirwa n’ibiza ikajyanwa mu mazu yubatswe ku buryo ahangana n’ingaruka z’imihindagurikire y’ibihe.

Isuzuma ryigenga ryagaragaje ko ibikorwa by’ubuhinzi buhangana n’imihindagurikire y’ibihe byateye imbere, umutekano w’ibiribwa ukarushaho kuba mwiza, ndetse n’ingo zikagira ubushobozi bwo guhangana n’ibibazo bitunguranye.

Icyakora, Minisitiri w’Intebe yavuze ko kongera ubushobozi bwo guhangana n’imihindagurikire y’ibihe bidahagije, kuko abahinzi bakeneye no kubona amasoko, inguzanyo n’amahirwe yo kwinjira mu ruhererekane rw’ibikorwa by’ubuhinzi bibyara inyungu. Yongeyeho ko abagore bagomba kugera kuri izo nyungu ku rugero rungana n’urw’abagabo.

Yagize ati: “Kugira ngo amafaranga abahinzi binjiza yiyongere, bakeneye kugera ku masoko, kubona igishoro no kwinjira mu ruhererekane rw’ibikorwa by’ubuhinzi; kandi inyungu zabyo zigomba kugera ku bagore kimwe n’abagabo.”

Yavuze ko u Rwanda rugomba kuva ku mishinga y’igerageza rukerekeza kuri gahunda nini ihuriweho, kuko imihindagurikire y’ibihe itita ku mbibi z’uturere.

Yagize ati: “Imihindagurikire y’ibihe ntireba imbibi z’ubuyobozi; u Rwanda ntirushobora guhangana na yo akarere kamwe kamwe.”

Gahunda ya kabiri y’Igihugu yo Kwihutisha Iterambere (NST2) n’Igishushanyo mbonera cya Gatanu cy'iterambere ry' Ubuhinzi (PSTA5) byihaye intego yo kongera umusaruro w’ibihingwa by’ibanze mu biribwa ku kigero kirenga 50% bitarenze mu 2029, guteza imbere urwego rw’ubuhinzi ku kigero kirenga 6% buri mwaka, ndetse no gukuba kabiri ibyoherezwa mu mahanga biva mu buhinzi n’ishoramari ry’abikorera muri uru rwego.

Ubuhinzi bugira uruhare rungana na hafi kimwe cya gatanu cy’umusaruro mbumbe w’u Rwanda, ariko intego ni ukubugira urwego rutanga umusaruro mwinshi, rukorera ku isoko kandi rushobora guhangana n’ingaruka z’imihindagurikire y’ibihe.

Minisitiri w’Intebe yavuze ko kugera kuri izi ntego bisaba gukemura imbogamizi zituma ishoramari mu buhinzi ritihuta, zirimo kuba abashoramari babona ubuhinzi bw’abahinzi bato nk’urwego rurimo ibyago byinshi, ndetse n’uturere tukaba tugikeneye kongererwa ubushobozi bwo gushyira mu bikorwa imishinga no kuyikomeza.

Yashimangiye ko nta soko rimwe ry’imari ryonyine ryabasha gutera inkunga iyi gahunda. Inkunga zitishyurwa zirakenewe mu gutegura imishinga no gufasha abaturage batishoboye, mu gihe inguzanyo zitangwa ku nyungu nto n’amabanki y’iterambere byafasha kugabanya ibyago no kwagura ishoramari.

Minisitiri w’Intebe yavuze ko u Rwanda rwiteguye kuva ku mishinga y’igerageza rukagera ku ishyirwa mu bikorwa ryagutse, hagamijwe kongera umusaruro w’ubuhinzi, kurinda imibereho y’abaturage no guhanga imirimo.

Yagize ati: “U Rwanda ruriteguye. Dufite icyerekezo, inzego n’ubunararibonye bidufasha kuva ku ntego tukagera ku ishyirwa mu bikorwa ku rwego runini. Nimukorane natwe, tuve ku mishinga y’igerageza tujye kuri gahunda zagutse, hanyuma tuzibyaze umusaruro ugaragara.”

L’Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) leaders including the Administrator of the OIF, Ms. Caroline St-Hilaire, and the President of the Summit Secretariat, Ms. Sophea EAT have this Thursday signed an agreement in the Cambodian capital, Phnom Penh.

The 20th edition of this Summit kicks off in the next three days.

This agreement concerns the OIF’s financial support to the Kingdom of Cambodge for organizing this major event.

The estimated budget for the 20th OIF Summit in Phnom Penh is close to €100 million based on costs for previous editions.

Insiders in the organisation said a large portion of the budget is allocated to security composed of 5,000 Cambodian personnel (police, gendarmerie, and army), 500 French and Canadian experts and Dedicated command centers, surveillance drones, and anti-drone barriers.

Cambodia’s Prime Minister Hun Manet said more than 20 countries confirmed that their top leaders, including heads of state, presidents and prime ministers, would attend the 20th Francophonie Summit scheduled for November 14 to 16.

The Cambodian Information Ministry reported earlier this week that 78 of the 90 expected countries had confirmed their participation.

French President Emmanuel Macron’s attendance will add significance to the occasion, as he will also make an official visit to Cambodia.

His visit will be the first by a French president to Cambodia in 60 years and only the second by a French head of state.

Ghana belatedly kick-started their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifying campaign with a 2-0 home win over Somalia.

The Black Stars had lost their opening two Group C matches against Ivory Coast and The Gambia, leading to the departure of coach Carlos Queiroz by mutual consent.

Ghana women's coach Kim Bjorkegren was placed in interim charge for this month's double-header against the Ocean Stars, with the West Africans in danger of missing a second successive edition of the Afcon finals.

The hosts were given a chance to take an early lead in Sekondi-Takoradi after Alidu Seidu was pulled down in the box, but Jordan Ayew's 14th-minute penalty was saved by Somalia goalkeeper Ibrahim Hussein.

Ghana did go ahead in first-half stoppage time when Mohammed Salisu headed Mohammed Kudus's deep corner back across goal and Jonas Adjetey nodded in from six yards out.

Felix Afena-Gyan doubled the Black Stars' advantage just after the hour mark when his shot from inside the box squirmed under Hussein and over the line.

The four-time continental champions remain six points behind group leaders Ivory Coast, who extended their 100% record by beating The Gambia 2-1 in Bouake.

Brighton midfielder Malick Yalcouye tucked in from seven yards out and Elye Wahi slotted home to double the Elephants' lead before Musa Barrow pulled one back for the visitors before the break.

Elsewhere on Thursday, there were wins for Cameroon, DR Congo and Senegal, who all remain on track to qualify for next year's tournament in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

The third round of qualifying fixtures continues on Friday with Egypt, Morocco, Nigeria and South Africa in action among 12 fixtures.

Nicolas Jackson has 11 goals in 17 appearances for club and country this season

Nicolas Jackson set Senegal on their way to a 4-1 home win over Sudan in Group J, with Aston Villa team-mate Ibrahim Mbaye also on the scoresheet for Patrick Vieira's men in Dakar.

The Teranga Lions lead the standings on seven points, three ahead of Mozambique, who host Ethiopia on Friday.

Cameroon also remained unbeaten and moved on to seven points in Group G with a comfortable 2-0 victory over Namibia in Douala.

Meanwhile, Newcastle United striker Yoane Wissa opened the scoring as DR Congo continued their perfect start with a 3-1 triumph over Sierra Leone in Kinshasa.

The Leopards are on nine points at the top of Group E, five points ahead of Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea after those two sides drew 0-0.

Nigeria were handed a boost after Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau could only manage a 1-1 draw in their away tie against Madagascar in neutral Morocco.

The Super Eagles trail Guinea-Bissau by four points ahead of their home game against Tanzania on Friday (16:00 GMT).

Tanzania are assured of a place at Afcon 2027 as tournament co-hosts, with the other three sides battling for one qualification spot.

And Benin bolstered their bid to reach back-to-back finals with a 4-1 win over Central African Republic.

Gernot Rohr's Cheetahs lead Group F by three points from Burkina Faso, who entertain Mauritania on Friday.

In Group D, another section with just one spot available, Guinea moved level on points with table-toppers South Africa after seeing off Eritrea 2-1 in Conakry.

Military cemetery decorum: The tradition behind Hegseth's Veterans Day reprimand

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has awarded a medal to the guard who reprimanded his group at Arlington National Cemetery.

A video of a Veterans Day observance event on Wednesday showed Hegseth, his wife and senior advisers laughing and talking while posing for photos in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier before the guard told them to be quiet.

In a statement, the Pentagon later announced that Hegseth had given Specialist Thomas Iglesias a Joint Service Commendation Medal "for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier".

Photos shared on the defence secretary's X account showed him presenting the medal to Iglesias.

He was accompanied by others whom the Pentagon identified as members of the 3rd US Infantry Regiment, known as the Old Guard, which is responsible for holding vigil over the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

"We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist. Carry on Patriots," the accompanying text on Hegseth's post reads.

In the video, the army sentinel on duty later identified as Iglesias can be seen stepping towards Hegseth's group and shouting: "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times."

Hegseth (right) awarding the medal to Specialist Iglesias

The Arlington National Cemetery etiquette requests that visitors speak quietly and do not engage in disrespectful or disorderly conduct.

The tomb, which is one of the country's most sacred war memorials, marks the final resting place of an unknown soldier who was killed in World War One, as well as a service person from World War Two and the Korea War. It also commemorates all missing service people from the Vietnam War.

Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said in a statement: "While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum.

"The Secretary and the entire Department have always honoured - and will always honour - the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe."

A service member from the 3rd Infantry Regiment stands watch over the tomb 24 hours a day and has done so since 1948.

It is not unusual for them to admonish visitors to the site, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News. They reportedly do so a few times a day.

Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and First Lady Melania Trump bow their heads in prayer during a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery

Earlier, President Donald Trump, Vice-President JD Vance and other top officials attended the annual wreath-laying at the cemetery.

During his speech at the ceremony, Trump offered his gratitude to uniformed service members who have fought for the country. He also touted what he sees as his administration's success in the Iran war.

Trump also pointed out Hegseth during the ceremony, saying he's done a "fantastic job" as defence secretary.

On Tuesday, an effort to impeach the defence secretary under accusations that he waged war on Iran without congressional authorisation failed on Capitol Hill .

Hegseth has called the impeachment efforts a "farce" and a "stunt".

If I'd told you this time last week that Jensen Huang was about to leave Nvidia, you would not have believed me.

The man who co-founded this enormously successful AI chip company, working tirelessly to build it from the ground up and steering it through some disastrous times with endless energy and ruthless determination, has ultimately been undone by his own love life.

It's an extraordinary tale and a strangely old fashioned one for a tech firm with its sights set on the future.

It spawned a plethora of viral memes, seeing Huang as the man caught by the Coldplay kiss-cam with a married colleague , or singing along to George Michael's classic hit about betrayal, Careless Whisper.

Both were ironically AI-generated using the very tech he was helping to build.

This week I met two Silicon Valley execs and I asked them how they were processing the news - "in memes", was the response.

But they didn't seem to think Huang would be forced out by his alleged adultery.

The stakes were too high, they said, the entire AI industry relies too heavily on Nvidia chips to break a winning formula.

In as many words, "the Valley" was on his side.

But that was before rumours of a second affair surfaced, this time with a colleague, and the board decided he had gone too far.

His behaviour suddenly cast him in a different light: a man who could make bad decisions and cover them up.

Huang always made a point of standing out from the crowd.

During the coronavirus lockdowns, he streamed keynote speeches from his kitchen (which gained internet fame in its own right, but were later revealed to have been AI-generated).

He is rarely seen without a leather jacket – he has joked that he only owns one suit, and he borrows his daughter's partner's tie.

Huang rubbed shoulders with the elite, with a network including Donald Trump, Elon Musk and King Charles.

The last time I saw him was at St James' Palace last year, where he was receiving the prestigious Queen's Prize for Engineering.

I was told he would not talk to the press - but he wandered over by himself and we spent about 10 minutes having a chat while press officers hovered nervously in the background. He was articulate and optimistic about the progress of AI and the UK's role in it.

For many people, Huang was Nvidia. He had as many as 200 people directly reporting to him.

He expected high standards – in his book about its inner workings, the Nvidia Way, author Tae Kim wrote the office hours were long.

Huang's feedback could be both brutal and public, and he thought nothing of pointing out individuals' mistakes in all-staff meetings.

Now it is his own shortcomings which are on very public display, and he has been forced into a brutal ending of his own career.

Colette Kress, who takes over for now, will be a familiar face internally and that must feel reassuring to some at Nvidia.

She's worked at the company for 13 years and for those who follow its considerable finances, she is often present on earnings calls. She is a billionaire in her own right and a high-flying tech executive.

But she's not an engineer and Nvidia's products are highly technical.

She will have to convince investors that it is business as usual for Nvidia, that the innovation for which it is renowned can continue at its existing pace, and that the top talent won't leave with Huang.

A wobbly Nvidia would be bad news for the entire AI industry because its ever-advancing chips drive the most powerful AI models, and it's also regarded as something of a central bank, loaning money to other firms.

As for Huang himself, we assume for now that the investigation into his relationship with the woman accused of being a Chinese spy will continue, and the results of that may well determine what he does next.

He probably won't be short of offers despite his conduct – and I expect Nvidia's rivals can't believe their luck that their formidable rival has taken himself out of the game. Elon Musk has already said it would be "an honour" to work with him at SpaceX.

It's important though to remember that even if Huang turns out not to have betrayed his company or his country, he still betrayed his wife of 41 years, Lori Huang.

And for her, it's not a story of tech, temptation and trillion-dollar-valuations.

Rwanda has increased its budget allocation to key social sectors by 4.2% to Rwf1.711 trillion for the 2026/2027 financial year, representing 22% of the country’s total national budget, according to a new report by UNICEF and the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning (MINECOFIN).

The report analyses public spending on education, health, social protection, and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), assessing the results achieved through investments in children and identifying areas requiring greater attention in the preparation of the 2027/2028 national budget.

The findings were presented in Kigali during an event jointly organised by UNICEF and MINECOFIN, bringing together government institutions and development partners to examine how public resources are being allocated to services that directly influence children’s well-being and long-term development.

The Rwf1.711 trillion allocation marks a 4.2% increase compared with the previous financial year, highlighting the government’s continued investment in essential social services.

However, the report also provides an opportunity to assess whether the increased spending is translating into improved access to quality education, healthcare, social protection and basic sanitation services.

By examining budget allocations alongside development outcomes, the analysis seeks to provide evidence that can guide policymakers in identifying spending priorities, addressing gaps and improving the effectiveness of public investment in children.

The report is expected to inform discussions on the 2027/2028 budget, particularly on how government resources can be better directed towards programmes that respond to children’s needs and support inclusive social development.

UNICEF and MINECOFIN emphasised the importance of using reliable data and budget analysis to strengthen public financial planning and ensure that investments in social sectors deliver measurable benefits to children and their families.

Pochettino was appointed USA manager in September 2024

Michael Carrick must have known what was coming.

Not just because reports of his imminent dismissal were widespread - followed by information about who would be replacing him as Manchester United boss.

But because, effectively, he and his representatives were given heavy enough indications of what was to follow.

On Monday, according to well-placed sources, Carrick's agent was contacted by chief executive Omar Berrada to be told he and director of football Jason Wilcox would be heading to Monaco for a planned meeting with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe that would include a discussion about the head coach's future.

A day later, it is believed Wilcox had a similar conversation with Carrick.

It is understood that on both occasions it was communicated that a recommendation regarding Carrick's future at the club would be made.

What is not clear is whether Carrick and his representatives knew that recommendation was to relieve him of his duties.

By that point, BBC Sport has been told United were aware of a $10m (£7m) release clause in Mauricio Pochettino's contract with the United States national team. One source even indicated it was representatives of the Argentine who told the Premier League side.

There is some regret behind the scenes at United that machinations leading to Carrick's departure on Thursday were played out so publicly.

But with football clubs the size of United, keeping such developments completely private is extremely difficult - and there is a feeling they were as transparent with Carrick as they could be.

Following heavy defeats by Como and Bournemouth , United placed huge importance on the following three games - against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa.

It is understood United's leadership team were clear with Carrick that results and performances needed to improve. A defeat, a victory and draw weren't enough to save him.

There is a feeling that during that three-game period, there was not enough progress, particularly in terms of team structure - underlined by the fact they conceded eight goals.

The chaos that took Carrick from two-year deal to sacked within 15 games

Carrick has conducted himself with great dignity during the turmoil of the past few days and he leaves the club - certainly in the eyes of supporters - with his standing as a United great intact.

When United first appointed Carrick - initially on an interim basis following the sacking of Ruben Amorim in January - he had a positive impact on the squad, and subsequently results.

United liked his positive messaging to the players and media. They felt Carrick brought calm to rocky waters and protected his players at every opportunity - a contrast from at least the closing stages of Amorim's tenure.

On the pitch, the United hierarchy felt Carrick's style of play allowed the forward players more freedom, and they won 12 of their last 17 matches of the season.

While United considered other managerial options in the summer, there was ultimately a sense Carrick had earned a shot at the job on a permanent basis.

The 45-year-old signed a two-year deal, though it is understood United contractually protected themselves in the event of an early termination.

Part of the thought process was to provide the players with some managerial stability given the increased turnover of head coaches in recent years.

Yet the season started poorly with defeat at newly promoted Hull City - and has only spiralled downward since.

United are third bottom of the Premier League and 17th in the Champions League table.

What does Mauricio Pochettino need to succeed at Manchester United?

Since Monday, talks have been ongoing with Pochettino.

On Wednesday, Berrada contacted the US Soccer Federation to confirm the existence of the release clause and their intention to activate it.

It is understood the news did not come as a surprise to those across the Atlantic.

Pochettino had been clear with his employers about the discussions with United and - most pertinently - his intention to return to the Premier League.

While United want Pochettino in situ as soon as possible, they are respectful of the fact the USA have two fixtures against Haiti to play - the second of which is on 18 November.

If Pochettino takes charge of the second game, it is understood he will be in place at United's Carrington headquarters on 19 November - four days before they face Liverpool.

Sosiyete y'ikoranabuhanga ya Nvidia yatangaje ko Jensen Huang yeguye ku mwanya wa Perezida akaba n'umuyobozi mukuru (CEO) wayo.

Ibi bibaye nyuma y'iminsi yari amaze ariho igitutu gishingiye ku makuru yavugaga ku guca inyuma uwo bashakanye, akagirana imibanire yihariye n'abagore babiri.

Bijya kumenyekana, ikinyamakuru The New York Times tariki 29 Ukwakira (10), cyanditse inkuru kivuga ko Huang yari afitanye umubano wa hafi na Alice Huang, umugore bamwe mu bayobozi ba Amerika bakeka ko ari intasi ikorera u Bushinwa.

Tariki 8 Ugushyingo (11), Jensen Huang yemeye ko yaciye inyuma umugore we, asaba imbabazi umuryango we, n'ubwo atatangaje uwo babikoranye.

Nyuma yaho, inama y'ubutegetsi ya Nvidia yahise itangiza iperereza ryigenga kuri icyo kibazo.

Bukeye bwaho, Perezida wa Amerika Donald Trump yavuze ko FBI irimo gukora iperereza kuri ayo makuru, mu gihe u Bushinwa bwahakanye bwivuye inyuma ayo makuru ndetse bunashimangira ko ibyo ari ugusebanya.

Ku wa 11 Ugushyingo, The New York Times yongeye gutangaza ko Huang yaba yaranagize indi mibanire yihariye n'umwe mu bayobozi b'isosiyete ya Nvidia.

Bivugwa ko inama y'ubutegetsi yahise iterana kugira ngo yige ku hazaza h'umuyobozi wayo.

Nyuma y'iyo nama, Nvidia yatangaje ko Huang, ufite imyaka 63, yeguye ku buyobozi bw'iyo sosiyete.

Umuyobozi ushinzwe imari muri Nvidia, Colette Kress, yahise agirwa umuyobozi mukuru w'agateganyo, mu gihe Harvey Jones wahoze ayobora Synopsys yagizwe perezida wa mbere w'inama y'ubutegetsi ya Nvidia.

Iyo nkundura yose yagize ingaruka ku isoko ry'imari, aho imigabane ya Nvidia yagabanutseho 13%, bituma agaciro k'isosiyete kajya munsi ya tiriyoni enye z'amadolari bwa mbere kuva muri Nyakanga(7) 2025.

Abasesenguzi bavuga ko ugusohoka kwa Huang gushyize Nvidia ndetse n'urwego rw'ubwenge buhangano(AI) mu kaga.

Mu gihe Perezida Donald Trump yamwise "umuntu w'inyangamugayo", bamwe mu bayobozi b'inteko ishingamategeko ya Amerika bo basabye ko hakorwa iperereza ryimbitse ku ngaruka z'iki kibazo ku mutekano w'Igihugu.

FC Andorra manager Carles Manso says goalkeeper Jesus Owono is yet to decide whether he will return to football following the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

Owono was sent off after colliding with De Miguel during a Spanish second division match on 2 November, with the Tenerife forward passing away the following day in hospital.

Manso said the goalkeeper, 25, is currently spending time with his family and is "completely free to make any decision" with regard to a potential return.

"What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him," Manso said.

"We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

"When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that [he will do so]."

Andorra released a statement on behalf of Owono on 4 November, with the Equatorial Guinea keeper saying he was experiencing "the most difficult days of my life".

He added: "I feel enormous pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him."

On Thursday, De Miguel's family released a statement via the Spanish Footballers' Association thanking those who had contributed to a crowdfunding page which has surpassed £170,000.

Fran Sol, a forward for Spanish third-tier side Hercules, set up the campaign with all proceeds going to relatives of De Miguel.

"We would like to express our heartfelt thanks for all the expressions of affection and support we have received," De Miguel's family said.

"We have been deeply moved to see so many of you rally behind this initiative."

Andorra will return to action for the first time since the forward's death on Saturday when they face Almeria in the Spanish second division.

Yabivuze kuri uyu wa Kane, ubwo Komisiyo y’Ubukungu n’Imari muri Sena yagezaga ku Nteko Rusange raporo y’igenzura yakoze ku gikorwa cya Guverinoma cyo kugeza amashanyarazi ku baturage.

Senateri Uwizeyimana yabajije Komisiyo niba, hashingiwe ku biganiro yagiranye n’inzego zifite amashanyarazi mu nshingano ndetse n’ingengabihe z’imishinga, ibona ko intego yo kugeza amashanyarazi kuri bose izagerwaho mu 2029.

Yagize ati “Njewe rero ndagira ngo mbaze Komisiyo niba, mwahuye na Minisitiri, mwahuye n’abantu bafite uru rwego mu nshingano, mukurikije ibiganiro mwagiranye n’ingengabihe babahaye, murabona iyo ntego izagerwaho? Mwebwe muri Komisiyo, njye ntabwo ndi bubabwire icyo mbitekerezaho.”

Yibukije ko intego ari uko kugeza mu 2029 ingo zose mu Rwanda zizaba zifite amashanyarazi, avuga ko hasigaye igihe gito cyo kuyigeraho.

Nubwo yari yabanje kuvuga ko adashaka gutangaza uko abona iki kibazo, Senateri Uwizeyimana yahise agaragaza impungenge afite, cyane cyane ku bijyanye n’ubwizerwe bw’umuriro ukwirakwizwa.

Yakomeje agira ati “Hari n’ibura ry’umuriro w’amashanyarazi rya hato na hato dukunze kubona na hano muri Kigali, cyane cyane iyo imvura iguye. Imvura iragwa ukagira ngo umuriro na wo ugiye kugama.”

Yatanze urugero rw’aho atuye mu Karere ka Kicukiro, avuga ko iyo imvura iguye umuriro ukunze kubura, ndetse ko iyo ahamagaye umukozi w’Urwego rw’Igihugu rushinzwe Ingufu (REG), asubizwa ko hari insinga z’amashanyarazi zaguye.

Senateri Uwizeyimana yavuze kandi ko ikibazo cy’ubuke bw’amashanyarazi gikunda kugaragara, cyane cyane mu bice birimo inganda, asanga gishobora kurushaho gukomera uko umubare w’ibinyabiziga bikoresha amashanyarazi uzagenda wiyongera.

Perezida wa Komisiyo y’Ubukungu n’Imari muri Sena, Senateri Fulgence Nsengiyumva, yavuze ko nta mpamvu yo gukeka ko intego yo kugeza amashanyarazi kuri bose itazagerwaho, ashingiye ku muvuduko igihugu kiriho mu kongera ubushobozi bwo kubyaza no gutanga amashanyarazi.

Yagaragaje ko mu 2024 u Rwanda rwari rufite ubushobozi bwo kubyaza amashanyarazi bungana na Megawatt 406, ariko ubu bukaba bumaze kugera kuri Megawatt 472.4.

Senateri Nsengiyumva yavuze ko hari n’imishinga umunani iri gukorwa, irimo ingomero, inganda n’imishinga y’amashanyarazi akomoka ku mirasire y’izuba, izongera ubushobozi bw’igihugu bwo kubona amashanyarazi ho Megawatt 523.

Visi Perezida wa Komisiyo y’Ubukungu n’Imari, Senateri Dr. Nyinawamwiza Laetitia, na we yavuze ko intego yo kugeza amashanyarazi kuri bose iri kugerwaho ku buryo bushimishije.

Ati “Ahubwo kugeza abaturage ku mashanyarazi ku gipimo cya 100% turimo kubikozaho imitwe y’intoki.”

Yavuze ko mu 2029 ubushobozi bw’amashanyarazi u Rwanda rufite buzaba bumaze kwikuba hafi inshuro ebyiri, mu gihe kuri ubu abaturarwanda bagerwaho n’amashanyarazi bangana na 88.3%.

Uganda Airlines is preparing to strengthen air connectivity between Rwanda and Uganda with the introduction of daily flights linking Kigali and Entebbe, in a move expected to boost tourism, trade, business travel and regional integration.

The new route, which officially launches on November 18, 2026, was presented at a travel trade engagement held at Kigali Serena Hotel on November 12, bringing together travel agents, tour operators and tourism stakeholders to explore opportunities for cooperation with the airline.

Speaking at the event, Lillian Kyategwa, Uganda Airlines Country Director, said the new service is intended to build on the longstanding relationship between the neighbouring countries while making the movement of people, goods and services across the region easier.

“Uganda Airlines has come to this market to strengthen the already good relationship between Rwanda and Uganda, while easing the movement of people, goods and services within the region and connecting us to the rest of the world,” Kyategwa said.

She noted that Rwanda’s growing reputation as a regional conference and business destination presents an important opportunity for the airline, particularly as demand for convenient regional connections continues to grow.

“Rwanda has become a hub for conferences, and we are ready for this market. Today was about meeting and strategising with ticketing agencies to see how we can work together with the airline,” she added.

The engagement provided an opportunity for Uganda Airlines to establish closer working relationships with travel agencies and tour operators in Rwanda, who are expected to play a key role in promoting the new service and connecting passengers to destinations beyond Entebbe.

Michael Bulwaka, Counsellor at the Uganda High Commission in Rwanda, said the new route reflects the strong connections between the two countries, which extend beyond geographical proximity.

He pointed to family ties, shared interests, business opportunities and a common development vision as some of the factors that continue to bring Rwanda and Uganda closer.

“The new flights will further strengthen cooperation between our two countries, promote trade, tourism and investment, and advance the spirit of East African integration,” Bulwaka said.

He emphasised that Uganda Airlines’ role goes beyond transporting passengers, describing the national carrier as an important instrument for representing Uganda and connecting the country to regional and international markets.

Bulwaka also encouraged Rwanda’s tourism and travel industry players to work closely with the airline, saying the new connection offers opportunities to expand their businesses and reach more customers.

For Uganda Airlines, the Kigali–Entebbe connection is also part of a broader ambition to make movement across Africa easier and strengthen economic relationships through aviation.

“A connected Africa is a stronger Africa. When our people, goods and ideas move freely between our countries, we grow together,” the airline said in a message highlighting the significance of the new route.

The airline further described the connection as an opportunity for businesses to access new markets, travellers to discover more destinations and families to enjoy shorter journeys between neighbouring countries.

Meanwhile, Shakila Rahim Lamar, Acting Chief Commercial Officer of Uganda Airlines, pointed to plans to expand the airline’s fleet, saying additional aircraft are expected to increase capacity and create room for more routes.

“More aircraft, more routes, more of Africa connected,” she said, noting that the expansion will offer passengers greater choice and open up additional travel opportunities across the continent and beyond.

The Kigali–Entebbe service is expected to benefit travellers connecting through Uganda to the airline’s wider international network, including destinations in Europe, Asia, the Middle East and Africa.

With daily flights beginning November 18, Uganda Airlines is positioning the new route as more than an additional air connection, but as another step towards strengthening regional trade, tourism and people-to-people relations.

For Rwanda and Uganda, the new air link is expected to make an already close relationship more accessible, creating new opportunities for businesses, travellers and the wider East African economy.

BBC's Samira Hussain reports from Wall Street on what the fall of the tech superstar means.

Jensen Huang, known for sporting a black leather jacket to shareholder events, appeared to have it all. He was courted by leaders in the US and China alike, worshipped by investors and seen as a loyal family man. But a rockstar approach to his personal life has ultimately led to his resignation.

The 63-year-old has been married since 1985, long before the foundation of Nvidia, the company that propelled him to tech stardom.

He is known as a workaholic and a demanding manager, with high standards for those who worked for him, which included his own children, promoted within the company. But he has seen his personal reputation go into freefall this week, undone by romantic entanglements that throw doubt on his focus and his judgement.

On Thursday, he resigned following back-to-back revelations of two affairs. News of the first - a relationship with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese spy - ricocheted around the world, raising eyebrows among investors. It was followed on Wednesday by reports that the tech boss had also had an affair with an Nvidia colleague.

His departure creates uncertainty in the global stock market, which was already knocked-off balance in recent weeks. Nvidia is a linchpin in the US's race for technology leadership with China.

Huang may not be a household name on the same level as Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg.

But his role in the tech industry, especially in relation to the explosion of artificial intelligence in the last three years, may prove more consequential. Nvidia dominates the market for the microchips that are used to power the new technology.

The company, which is still valued at nearly $4n (£3.02tn) despite recent events, is at the centre of the AI race between the US and China, the world's tech and economic powerhouses.

Huang enjoyed access to the seats of political power on an unrivalled scale, being courted by both US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping.

His remarkable rise to the top of his profession has led to him being dubbed the "Taylor Swift of tech" and seen him amass an estimated fortune of $145bn, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

Despite always donning his trademark all-black outfits and taking a playful approach to investor presentations, Huang has worked for years to present himself as a family man, someone who exemplified the American Dream.

Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang and his family moved to the west coast of the US when he was nine years old. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a Master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.

It was at college where he met his wife, Lori Mills. The pair were lab partners and married in 1985, eight years before Huang founded Nvidia.

They have two children, Madison and Spencer, who now both work in senior roles at Nvidia.

The company became a key provider of the computer chips and circuits used for gaming before it expanded in a new direction. It now creates the key processing chips used to power the growing AI technology.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after tech giant rocked by second affair allegation

Who could replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia's chief executive?

Huang has hailed AI as a "new industrial revolution" that is on par with the advent of electricity. Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company and its customers include the biggest firms on the planet, Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, SpaceX, Tesla, OpenAI and Anthropic, all spending big on its products.

So it is no surprise that at a recent AI summit at the White House, Huang was picked out from a group of 42 to flank the president, alongside Elon Musk, both men with whom Trump has famously close relationships.

"Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on Jensen Huang, told the BBC, referring to the late boss of Apple. He added that Huang was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today.

He described him as a "demanding" boss, who "really pushes his people to the limit".

But while the former Nvidia CEO is "very brilliant" and a "world-class computer scientist", there's also "a level of arrogance" and "a level of self-deception as well", he said.

Huang had gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, he added, something that was "very important to him".

"He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways," Witt added. "The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad."

First reports emerged on 29 October in the New York Times that Huang had conducted a relationship with Alice Huang, no relation. US officials allege the businesswoman associated with Singapore-based firm Megaspeed is a Chinese intelligence asset.

After the revelations of the first affair, Huang admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting their family.

Trump, as well as other leaders in the AI tech industry, initially backed Huang to continue in his role at Nvidia. The president described him as "honourable".

But the reporting of a second affair, with Kimberly Powell, vice president of healthcare who has worked at Nvidia for 18 years, prompted a board meeting, followed by the announcement Huang was stepping down.

In the aftermath of that news Trump said Huang had done "a fantastic job" and proposed Tim Cook of Apple as a suitable replacement at the head of Nvidia.

Why Democrat Scott Colom’s win in Mississippi Senate race is so significant

After winning a close race in Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom will become the state's first black US senator for more than 150 years, and the third in history.

It is a historic result in the deeply conservative southern state that last sent a Democrat to the US Senate in 1982, and had not seated a black senator since 1875.

Colom follows Hiram Revels, who became the first black person ever to serve in the chamber when he was seated from 1870 to 1871, and Blanche Bruce, whose term ran from 1875 to 1881. Revels and Bruce were both members of the Republican Party.

Revels was chosen as Mississippi's first senator after the Civil War, serving for just over a year and campaigning strongly for racial equality.

A few years later, Bruce, who was born into slavery, became the first black person to serve a full term in the US Senate. He remained in Washington after leaving the chamber and held a role in the Treasury.

Both terms came before the repressive Jim Crow laws began to enforce racial segregation across Mississippi and other southern US states.

Blanche Bruce (L) and Hiram Revels (R) are the two previous black senators to have been chosen by Mississippi

A significant factor in Colom's victory was his success in mobilising young people and the state's large black population, who are expected to have turned out in high numbers.

In a victory speech, Colom referenced how Revels, who was a minister and served as a chaplain during the Civil War, gained support for his Senate campaign through his words.

"That's an example of the power of prayer, and through our history, there are so many people that lifted this state up through the power of prayer in very dark times," Colom said.

A portrait of Hiram Revels, taken in about 1870

Prior to the result being called, the BBC spoke to students at Jackson State University, a historically black college in Mississippi. Many of them had voted for the first time and backed Colom.

"I really feel like a change is what we need," 18-year-old Jamyria Dunn said.

"I've had some amazing days in my life," she continued, "but seeing Mississippi, this state in particular, turn blue, would really bring a light to my heart that people just would not understand."

Colombia's president said one of 10 "priority targets" was among those killed

A senior leader of Colombia's largest criminal gang, the Gulf Clan, is among eight people killed in an air strike carried out by the country's armed forces, according to President Abelardo de la Espriella.

De la Espriella said he had personally authorised the bombing targeting the Gulf Clan in the province of Antioquia, in north-west Colombia.

He added that Haminton Mosquera, whom he described as a senior member of the crime gang and one of 10 "priority targets" for Colombia's security forces, had been "brought down".

De la Espriella was elected in June after campaigning on a promise to crack down on Colombia's powerful criminal gangs, including by launching air strikes.

In a post on X , external , he said that Mosquera was suspected of having ordered attacks against the security forces, including the murder of a police officer in the municipality of Tarazá last year.

The Gulf Clan has been engaging in criminal activities for decades, mainly trafficking cocaine from Colombia to destinations in the US and Europe but also illegal mining and people smuggling.

The US added it to its list of Foreign Terrorist Organisations (FTOs) last year.

In his post, President de la Espriella said that "the offensive won't stop" and vowed to regain control of areas currently controlled by criminal organisations such as the Gulf Clan.

While his offensive against criminal gangs has been welcomed by many living in areas where extortion and gang violence are rampant, de la Espriella has faced criticism for the way he has made some of his announcements on security.

Less than a month after taking office, he published a video showing him walking among 23 body bags containing the remains of 23 people killed in an air strike on a suspected guerrilla camp.

On Wednesday, he shared a photo , external in which he can be seen writing his campaign slogan, "Welcome to the miracle homeland" on a bomb.

He has also defended his decision to wear an army uniform at a recent event in Cúcuta at which he confronted a detainee suspected of being a Farc rebel.

"What did you make of the bomb I sent you, signed by me?," the president can be heard asking the man.

He later told journalists that he wore the uniform because "I am a soldier of the homeland. That's why I dress like a soldier, because I came to serve Colombia. Because I honour the heroes, police officers and military."

Additional reporting by BBC Monitoring's Luis Fajardo.

Russell Brand's social media accounts on platforms owned by tech company Meta have been disabled.

It comes after the 51-year-old former entertainer was sentenced to 10-and-a-half-years in jail for one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault earlier this week.

He was found guilty of the charges involving four women and relating to offences between 2004 and 2009.

Meta owns social media platforms including Instagram and Facebook.

Brand is currently in prison and is expected to serve seven years of his sentence behind bars before being released on licence.

On Wednesday evening, a post appeared on his X account, which remains active. "There was never a Russell Brand, according to @meta," it read.

"Thank God for @elonmusk," the message added, referring to X's owner. "Stay tuned," it concluded.

The post included what appeared to be screenshots showing Brand's Instagram account having been disabled.

Meta's community standards policy says that "in order to maintain a safe environment and empower free expression" it restricts or removes accounts that are "harmful to the community".

That includes accounts owned by convicted sex offenders.

In 2023, after a media investigation revealing allegations about Brand's behaviour - which he denies - YouTube suspended his channels from making money from adverts for "violating" its "creator responsibility policy".

At the time, the video platform said it was taking action "to protect" its users.

The UK economy grew at its fastest rate for more than two years in the three months to September.

"Top gear" and "strikingly strong" were among the descriptions of the 0.7% growth offered by the economists who track every minor murmur of Britain's economy.

It is an upgrade on "solid" and "resilient", and in turn a world away from "hardest hit by the Iran War".

Against the backdrop of the world's biggest disruption to energy flows, rising market borrowing costs - and the cruel summers since the pandemic - it is impressive growth.

It should reset some of the swirl of self-reinforcing negativity.

The UK's economic growth has averaged less than 0.1% in the four Q3s [ie July to September] since the pandemic.

The average prediction just months ago for this July to September was just 0.1%.

Even the UK's official forecaster the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) effectively pencilled in 0.3% at the Budget just 3 weeks ago.

This figure has not been exceeded outside the pandemic since 2017. It puts the UK on course to be the second fastest growing economy after the US across the major G7 countries which also includes Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy and France.

It is tempting to think about what the economy would have done if the Iran War hadn't happened. If interest rates had been cut instead of their recent rise.

While the latest figure kills the doom, it is clearly not a boom either.

Spending on AI and tech have driven the surprise upside over the year. While the AI data centre boom may at any point turn to bust, these figures suggest that spending across the economy on investing in these technologies is helping to boost growth. Consumers have been resilient, at least till the autumn, perhaps helped by better economic vibes.

While there has been an understandable focus on high UK borrowing costs, another measure of the international standing of the UK economy, sterling's value, reached post Brexit referendum highs last week.

Productivity and investment is also looking stronger, especially after recent revisions. Some of the most encouraging figures are in private sector business investment.

I spoke to the chancellor at Nexeon in Oxfordshire, which is searching for a UK factory to manufacture its cutting edge electric vehicle battery - and British - technology. My colleagues visited British watchmakers in Maidenhead carving out a niche to take on the Swiss.

However, this may well not last for the final three months of the year.

Consumer confidence has already fallen as petrol and domestic energy prices start to rise again.

There is a significant challenge with everyday cost-of-living pressures in the coming months. Construction and private house building remain depressed.

The Iran conflict remains the big unknown and whether post the US midterm elections there could be a durable end to the conflict in the Gulf.

Some oil and gas production there is starting to normalise. It could bring down petrol prices, energy bills, government borrowing costs, and mortgage costs too.

Expect to see Downing Street investing heavily in "settlement of the conflict", which the chancellor told me is the "best economic policy".

Billy Vigar died from a "significant brain injury" in September 2025

The police investigation into the death of former Arsenal academy player Billy Vigar is ongoing, a coroner's court has heard.

Vigar died from a "significant brain injury" in September 2025, five days after colliding with a concrete wall surrounding a pitch while playing for Chichester City at Wingate and Finchley's stadium.

His parents, Keith and Camilla, told BBC Sport on the one-year anniversary that "the FA could have stopped Billy losing his life because they had so many warnings".

Acting Detective Sergeant Colin Chandler, from the Metropolitan Police, told a pre-inquest review hearing that he anticipated he would need another "two to three months" on his investigation.

He did not provide details on the lines of enquiry that the police are exploring.

BBC Sport has contacted the Met for comment.

Vigar's parents were present for the hearing at Barnet Coroner's Court on Thursday, as were representatives from the Football Association and Barnet Council.

Former Bath City player Alex Fletcher, who fractured his skull when colliding with concrete barriers next to the club's pitch in 2022, was also present, as was PFA representative Adam White.

Camilla Vigar told senior coroner Andrew Walker: "I don't understand how the FA waited for Billy to die before they actioned anything when there was so much warning beforehand.

"Ben Hiscox dying in 2015. Alex had his big accident in 2022. The investigation they did after that highlighted about 160 high-risk clubs. Wingate was one of them. They did nothing."

Keith Vigar spoke during the hearing to raise an "issue with Barnet not being an interested party" in the case.

"Personally I don't quite understand how the investigation carried out at the football club, Wingate and Finchley... I see it as a bit of a conflict of interest that Barnet as the local authority carried out that investigation. It feels like they are marking their own homework," he said.

A further hearing has been scheduled for 10 February.

Min says people do not always understand her sacrifices and how valuable support is

A young carer says she feels burnt out, and forgotten about by friends as she takes on extra tasks at home.

Madeline, 16, from Bridgend, cares for her mum and granddad, a role she says she is happy to do.

But she has said people do not always understand its mental impact, and believes both formal and informal support is "crucial" to young people.

She is one of an estimated 170,000 young carers in the UK aged five to 17, but the Carers Trust calls that number the "tip of the iceberg" , external .

The Welsh government said its latest strategy, which is expected to be published this month, had a particular focus on young carers and recognises their contributions.

Madeline, also known as Min, is one of 8,200 young carers in Wales. The 2021 census said there were about 120,000 young carers in England and 42,000 in Scotland.

She is still at school and hopes to be a paediatric doctor one day.

"For me, being a young carer involves helping my mum get up in the mornings, making sure my mum and my granddad have had their medication," she said.

"It also involves cooking meals for my mum, my granddad or my siblings.

"There's also the cleaning which I'll do, any household job really no matter what it is."

She said it can be difficult and often people do not understand what being a young carer entails.

"I find that my friends that aren't young carers don't tend to understand and that I can't always go out when they want or stay out to a certain time so I get kind of pushed aside and forgotten by my own friends," she added.

"Then there's the mental like side effects and stuff because obviously I'm caring about everyone else and I don't often tend to have time for myself."

Min says friends struggle to understand the role of young carers

Min said support, both formal and informal, "means the world" to young people like her.

When she was eight, Min was referred to Bridgend Carers' Centre, which is partly funded by Children In Need , external , which gives her respite and a chance to socialise with other young carers.

Without this, and support at school, Min said she "couldn't cope".

She said: "The young carers' group is so important to me because all my close friends that actually know what I go through, I get to see in these groups.

"They take us out places which I don't actually tend to do with my mum and my granddad because they're both so heavily disabled, so it's more for me to get out and express myself to be able to spend some time away from what I do."

Min will take part in the annual Children in Need choir which brings together young people supported by its projects from across the UK, singing a mash-up on the night.

She said: "It's shocking [to be] one of a handful of kids to be chosen, it's like, I'm one of the only people that are gonna be able to say I've sung with Children in Need and I'm so excited to be a part of it.

"It's going to be such a memorable experience, I just can't wait."

Alissa Bevan (left) and Erika Stevens (centre) are youth workers at Bridgend Carers Centre, whose support Madeline says "means the world"

Min's mum Rebecca said she was "so proud" of her daughter and said support from the group had been the "making of her".

"It has opened her whole life up," she said.

"She's learnt lots of new things, mainly it's confidence and friendships, it's definitely made her a more rounded person, other people her age didn't quite fit with her because they didn't understand, but with the young carers groups, they all understand.

"I know that she doesn't ever see it as an extra responsibility, it's just what she does for her family, for us, because she loves me, she loves us, and she likes to be a caring person."

Alissa Bevan manages the group Min attends and said it was important to see young carers recognised.

"Min's confidence has grown massively," she said.

"She was very shy and timid, not that you would believe that now, and she's made so many really good friends from this group as well.

'It's just a chance for them to be children and not have to worry about all the other responsibilities that they've got a home and come and just have an hour for themselves.

"They're selfless and they give so much."

A Welsh government spokesperson said: "Young carers make a huge contribution to their families and communities. But caring should not affect their education or social opportunities.

"Our National Strategy for Unpaid Carers, published later this month, has a particular focus on young carers.

"We have worked with young carers, councils and support services to identify the action required so that young carers are recognised and they and their families get the help they need."

Kinshasa put forward Juliana Amato Lumumba, a former Minister of Culture and daughter of the late Prime Minister Patrice Emery Lumumba

The Francophone world has its eyes on the 20th Francophonie Summit in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, where the next Secretary-General of the Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) will be elected on November 16.

But Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi has made it his personal mission to sabotage the vote, driven openly by his anti-Rwanda sentiment. He wants a Congolese candidate at the helm of the OIF for the next mandate. And should that ambition fail, he is threatening to pull the Democratic Republic of Congo out of the organization.

What is remarkable about this story is the consistent pattern Kinshasa, under the Tshisekedi administration, adopts: it divides every single organization it belongs to. It either gets its way or it disrupts the whole structure.

In February 2026, Kinshasa put forward Juliana Amato Lumumba, a former Minister of Culture and daughter of the late Prime Minister Patrice Emery Lumumba, with the stated aim of challenging the incumbent Secretary-General, Louise Mushikiwabo. One would have thought a fair fight was in the cards, and that the loser would stand down graciously. One would have been wrong.

Kinshasa poured millions of dollars into convincing several member states to support Lumumba’s candidacy. Yet the campaign, poorly conceived and driven more by anti-Rwanda sentiment than by a credible vision for the organization, quickly ran aground.

Lumumba herself has recently expressed frustration, accusing Kinshasa of abandoning her in the race. She understands that her candidacy has not received the necessary support, lobbying or political commitment from the very people who put her forward.

Now, with the election approaching and the prospects of victory looking increasingly slim for Tshisekedi’s camp, a new tactic has emerged: threatening to withdraw the DRC from the OIF.

During his visit to Kinshasa, French Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs Jean-Noël Barrot met Tshisekedi, who threatened that the DRC would leave the organization if Louise Mushikiwabo were re-elected. The same threat was repeated by Congolese government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya in a recent interview with Global Africa Télésud.

This is where Kinshasa’s campaign lost the contest. From the outset, the regime was fighting a losing battle by choosing to challenge a highly competent and experienced Secretary-General, not on the basis of her performance or qualifications, but largely because she is Rwandan.

Kinshasa’s goal is now clear: divide the bloc and force a stalemate in which the organization remains dysfunctional should it not heed its latest tantrum.

The same tactic was used within the East African Community (EAC), where Kenya and Uganda supported negotiations while Burundi and Tanzania backed war against the rebels in exchange for promises of millions of dollars.

Kinshasa equally divided the SADC community, with only South Africa and Malawi choosing the promised financial rewards and sending troops in support of the regime while the rest refused to get involved. Both the EAC and SADC are now sidelined in the search for a solution to the Congolese crisis, and Kinshasa owes money in unpaid contributions to both.

Similarly, the AU and the UN have become battlegrounds for Kinshasa’s campaign to impose its narrative of the crisis, a narrative in which it portrays itself as a victim without ever mentioning the peace agreement it signed in Washington, which committed it to end its alliance with a genocidal group, the FDLR, and to neutralize that group.

Now it is the OIF’s turn. And as delegates prepare to gather in Phnom Penh, one wonders whether the hundred delegates Tshisekedi is bringing to Cambodia, coupled with his threat to withdraw from the OIF, will move the needle.

Will the OIF really refuse to crown the undisputed winner of these elections just to appease a regime that arms a genocidal group?

MSF says that many frontline workers do not have the equipment they need

Hundreds of millions of dollars meant to help tackle Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo are not reaching the intended recipients, a medical charity has warned.

A report from Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) said that while the outbreak remained "out of control", front-line workers were going unpaid, lacked proper training and were struggling with shortages of essential supplies.

It added that in some cases ambulances had run out of fuel.

More than 5,400 people have died and 11,000 infected with Ebola in DR Congo since the outbreak was declared in May.

This makes it the second-most deadly outbreak of the disease ever recorded.

MSF has urged the Congolese government and UN agencies to "strengthen oversight and accountability" to ensure money already disbursed is effectively utilised.

This means "ensuring response personnel are properly trained, paid, equipped, and supported, and directing resources towards areas where needs are greatest", it said.

The BBC has asked the Congolese government for comment.

MSF's warning adds to concerns raised by Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) last month, when it said that $700m (£527m) out of $962m disbursed to organisations implementing Ebola response was unaccounted for.

At the time, Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya said it was too early to describe it as embezzlement, characterising the issue as a major transparency and financial reporting failure.

The Congolese health minister echoed these concerns, saying that aid agencies were required to provide details of their work so the ministry could provide oversight but that only 22% had done so.

"Our requirement is clear: transparency must be total. The response relies on a single plan, a single budget, and a single coordination," Health Minister Samuel-Roger Kamba said on X. , external

What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?

In its report , external , the charity said: "Despite the vast amounts of money provided for the response, many frontline responders are left trying to contain the outbreak with empty hands and empty pockets."

It also mentioned Ebola monitoring "surveillance teams that exist on paper but are nowhere to be seen on the ground".

"Our teams are often left speechless by the dysfunctions they witness in many areas. Six months into the response, this situation is simply unacceptable," said MSF president Javid Abdelmoneim.

One important way of stopping Ebola from spreading is contact tracing - finding all those people who had come into contact with an infected person and putting them into isolation.

"Despite the resources officially allocated to this critical activity, surveillance remains deeply problematic," MSF said, adding that two-thirds of deaths were occurring in communities not treatment centres.

According to British epidemiologist Neil Ferguson, more than half of the cases are going undetected, meaning the outbreak is likely to last another year, reports the Reuters news agency.

MSF also raised concerns over "excessive concentration" of efforts in certain areas at the expense of other areas where needs were more urgent.

It said the response was "too slow" in North Kivu province while Haut-Uélé remained "dramatically overlooked".

In both provinces, MSF observed that teams were "inadequately resourced to respond effectively" with health facilities lacking essential items such as water, chlorine or triage systems.

"This has turned some facilities into new centres of transmission, rather than places of care that contribute to containing the disease," MSF said.

The epicentre of the outbreak is in eastern DR Congo, which has been wracked by conflict for many decades, with some affected areas under rebel control.

There are very few good roads in the area, making it very hard to travel around.

On Thursday, the UN and government warned that the areas worst affected by Ebola were also suffering from a severe food crisis, with almost 10 million in the region in dire need.

The latest outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo species of the virus, has spread beyond DR Congo borders, with cases reported in Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria.

On Wednesday, the last person infected with Ebola in Kenya was discharged, marking a major milestone in efforts to contain the disease in the East African nation .

The Bundibugyo species is relatively rare and has no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.

Barbara Broccoli will be the first female president in the National Film and Television School's history

A producer whose credits include the James Bond movies has been announced as the first female president of a film school.

Barbara Broccoli will take over the role at the UK's National Film and Television School (NFTS) in Beaconsfield, Buckinghamshire, in February, succeeding Oscar-winning producer David Puttnam.

She has produced nine Bond films with her half-brother, Michael G. Wilson, before it was announced in February that Amazon MGM Studios had gained creative control.

Puttnam, whose credits include Chariots of Fire, The Killing Fields and Midnight Express, said he was "over the moon" that such a "hugely respected figure" was succeeding him.

The National Film School was established in 1971 by director Colin Young, taking over the Beaconsfield site with an initial intake of about 25 students.

In 1982 the institution was renamed the National Film and Television School to reflect its expanding curriculum.

Puttnam, who has been involved with the school for over 50 years, said it was a "lovely job" to have and that he had tried never to interfere.

He added that Broccoli's decision to take up the role was a "wonderful thing for the school".

Puttnam will take on an honorary role as president emeritus.

Daniel Craig previously praised Broccoli's "passionate and protective determination"

News of Broccoli's appointment comes ahead of the opening in January of the Cubby Broccoli Building at the school's Beaconsfield campus.

The building is named after Broccoli's father, the producer Albert R. "Cubby" Broccoli, who established the James Bond franchise.

The school said its expansion , external will provide 25,000 sq ft of additional teaching space, house new courses in costume design and hair and make-up, expand apprenticeship opportunities and provide purpose-built accessible student accommodation for the first time in its history.

Some schools have removed David Walliams books from their libraries following the publication of allegations against the best-selling children's author and comedian.

"Head teachers are already making difficult decisions about whether or not these books should remain on the bookshelves of libraries at the moment," said Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders.

"I'm aware from several of our members that they've already taken the decision to take them off their shelves."

Walliams sold more than 50 million copies of books including Gangsta Granny and Billionaire Boy. He has denied allegations of sexual misconduct and abuses of power.

Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Mr Di'Iasio urged the government to give schools national guidance, so they are "not leaving this open to one or two head teachers making one decision and others making a different one".

Darren Morgan, head of Kings Road Primary School in Manchester, told the programme that he has taken the decision to remove Walliams' publications.

The stories have been useful to promote reading, but "when there are these allegations it's really difficult to keep these books on the shelves", he said.

Steve Chalke, head of Oasis Academies, which runs more than 50 schools, said it was impossible to stop children seeing the current stories about Walliams.

"So when a child wanders into a school and into the library and sees his name or perhaps sees his photograph on a book, it can be very traumatising for some children," he said.

Author Chloe Combi, who has written about "how it feels to be young in modern Britain" and Generation Z, said banning Walliams' books is not appropriate, and could mean that important conversations about him "get swept under the carpet".

"I think by talking about it and what has happened - and the responsibility of parents to have that conversation with their kids - that actually makes more sense," she told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"I'm totally sympathetic with schools for withdrawing him and bookshops withdrawing him as an individual decision. But the point is, none of that is going to erase what's happened."

The Department for Education has been asked for comment.

Retailers including Waterstones, TG Jones, and The Works, say they will no longer sell Walliams' books, and his publisher HarperCollins cut ties with him in September.

Public libraries have also faced calls to remove his books.

Librarians' body CILIP said it "recognises that dealing with challenges made to books or other resources can be an extremely complex and stressful situation for library staff".

Decisions about stocking books are made by local councils.

Among them, Kent County Council said it had no plans to remove Walliams' titles from its libraries.

"The starting point is that books should be available to readers unless their content is unlawful," a spokesperson said.

"Decisions about library stock are not made through blanket bans on individual authors. Collections are regularly reviewed and refreshed to reflect factors such as reader demand, condition and relevance of stock."

A Telford and Wrekin council spokesperson added that after the "recent media coverage and allegations published in the press" they had taken the decision to "remove all Walliams' books and audio books from their library catalogues".

Surrey County Council said that demand for Walliams' books had "fallen significantly in recent years", but his titles are "not illegal" and "remain available for readers to borrow".

Camden Council in north London said it was putting Walliams' books in storage.

A spokesperson told the Camden New Journal: "We are committed to making Camden a safer place for women and girls, to challenging harmful attitudes, and promoting healthy relationships.

"Following these allegations, we believe the most appropriate action is to remove these books from display."

On Tuesday, ITV News and the Guardian published reports alleging that Walliams has been accused of sexual misconduct by several women, including some who accused him of "grooming" them when they were teenagers.

In a letter to journalists published by the paper, Walliams said he was "not a sexual predator" and had not "broken the law".
