Bomb squads have searched many schools but no devices have been found

Schools across Italy have received bomb threats for the second day in a row, sparking fresh panic and evacuations.

Some 3,778 schools, from Milan in the north to Sicily in the south, reported similar threats to one that created chaos on Wednesday - even though no explosive devices have been found.

The government has advised schools that "in the absence of concrete evidence beyond the simple receipt of a mass email indicating a danger, buildings must not not be evacuated". Unlike a day earlier, only 77 schools were evacuated on Thursday, authorities say.

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni says her government will come up with "sector-specific" advice to help those facing this kind of threat.

Schools in Scotland and Northern Ireland received threats on Wednesday, too. It is unclear whether the incidents are connected.

On Thursday morning, a bomb alert at a Calais rail station delayed international and national train services in northern France.

The latest incidents follow a series of bomb hoaxes last week against airports and airlines in a number of European countries.

Although a number of threats were claimed by an extremist misogynistic group, it later denied any link to the false warnings.

Wednesday's email threat - sent to 6,300 out of a total of 7,476 Italian state schools - was said to be from a certain "Mikhail Andropov, leader of Vilayat di Misoginistan".

Some officials say it originated in Taiwan.

A similar message sent to Italian schools on Thursday, again signed by Mikhail Andropov, is said to have been sent from the account of a teacher in the Philippines whose account is believed to have been hacked.

Grace Ashcroft, one of two playable protagonists in Resident Evil Requiem, was portrayed by Angela Sant'Albano, who won best lead performer

Resident Evil Requiem and its makers have won big at the Golden Joystick Awards, which celebrate the year's most popular games.

Released in February, it was the latest instalment of the global survival horror phenomenon, which has also spawned books, films and TV programmes since it was first released 30 years ago.

At Wednesday's awards ceremony, it scooped ultimate game of the year, console game of the year, best game trailer, and best lead performer for the game's star Angela Sant'Albano, who plays protagonist Grace Ashcroft.

Meanwhile its makers, Japanese studio Capcom, was named studio of the year and was also recognised for other games, including Onimusha: Way of the Sword and Pragmata.

FBI agent Grace Ashcroft was a brand new lead character in Resident Evil Requiem who, along with returning fan favourite Leon S. Kennedy, explores old haunts, such as Racoon City's police department as they investigate a series of mysterious deaths.

Securing 17% of the public vote, it was named ultimate game of the year ahead of other contenders Phantom Blade Zero, Crimson Desert, Control Resonant and The Blood of Dawnwalker.

Resident Evil Requiem won four awards including ultimate game of the year

There were prizes across 25 categories up for grabs - 22 of which are decided by a public vote amongst gamers from around the world.

While streamers' choice, critics' choice and developers' choice award are decided by critics.

Two of those went to indie hit Meccha Chameleon, a multiplayer hide-and-seek game where players paint themselves to blend in with their surroundings to evade others playing as hunters.

As well as streamers' choice and developers' choice, it also bagged best multiplayer game and best indie game - self published, which were chosen by the public.

Big Walk - a co-operative online game produced by Australian developer House House - was named critics' choice winner.

The studio was criticised this week after reports it used generative AI in the final stretch of the game's development , external - something it did not disclose at the time of the its release.

It said the tool was used to produce a tiny amount of code.

Minisiteri y’Imari n’Igenamigambi (MINECOFIN), yagaragaje ko u Rwanda rwifuza kurushaho gushimangira umuhigo wo gutegura igenamigambi no kugena ingengo y’imari hitabwa ku bana, no kureba ko umutungo wa Leta ukoreshwa mu buryo busubiza neza ibikenewe n’uburenganzira bwabo.

Ni bimwe mu byatangajwe kuri uyu wa Kane, tariki 12 Ugushyingo, ubwo ubuyobozi bw’iyo Minisiteri, n’Ishami ry’Umuryango w’Abibumbye ryita ku Burezi (UNICEF), bahuriraga mu gikorwa cyo gushyira ahagaragara raporo isesengura ingengo y’imari igenerwa inzego z’imibereho y’abaturage, zirimo uburezi, ubuzima, imibereho myiza y’abaturage, amazi, isuku n’isukura (WASH), igaragaza umusaruro umaze kugerwaho binyuze mu ishoramari rishyirwa mu bana, n’ibikwiye kwitabwaho mu gutegura ingengo y’imari ya 2027/2028.

Raporo yashyizwe ahagaragara isesengura ingengo y’imari y’umwaka wa 2026/2027, igaragaza ko amafaranga agenerwa izo nzego enye yiyongereyeho 4.2% agera kuri miliyari 1.711,3 Frw, bingana na 22% by’ingengo y’imari yose y’igihugu.

Iyi raporo ije mu gihe Guverinoma y’u Rwanda yatangiye imyiteguro y’ingengo y’imari y’umwaka wa 2027/2028, bityo ikaba izafasha mu kumenya ibyagezweho, ibibazo bigihari n’ahakwiye gushyirwa imbaraga kugira ngo amafaranga ashorwa muri izo nzego arusheho gutanga umusaruro.

Ingengo y’imari y’u Rwanda ya 2026/2027 ingana na miliyari 7.796,3 Frw, ikaba yariyongereyeho 12.1% ugereranyije n’umwaka ushize.

Iyi raporo inagaragaza ko kuba biteganyijwe ko izamuka ry’ibiciro rizagera kuri 10.5% muri uyu mwaka, hakwiye kwitabwa ku gaciro nyako k’amafaranga agenerwa inzego zagaragajwe, kugira ngo ubushobozi bwayo bwo gutanga serivisi ku bana butagabanuka.

Umuyobozi uhagarariye UNICEF mu Rwanda, Lieke van de Wiel, yagaragaje ko ishoramari rihoraho mu bana rimaze gutanga umusaruro ufatika.

Yagize ati: “U Rwanda rwerekanye ibyo ishoramari rihoraho mu bana rishobora kugeraho. Abana bapfa batarageza ku myaka itanu baragabanutse, abana benshi barangiza amashuri abanza, kandi imiryango myinshi yavuye mu bukene.”

Yavuze ko kurinda ishoramari rishyirwa mu bana mu gihe hategurwa ingengo y’imari ya 2027/2028, ari imwe mu nzira zizewe zo kubaka abakozi bafite ubuzima bwiza n’ubumenyi bukenewe kugira ngo icyerekezo cy’igihugu cya 2050 kizagerweho.

Raporo igaragaza ko u Rwanda rukomeje kongera ubushobozi bwo gutanga serivisi zifitiye abana akamaro, binyuze mu kongera amafaranga ava imbere mu gihugu akoreshwa mu nzego z’imibereho y’abaturage.

Mu burezi, amafaranga akoreshwa aturutse imbere mu gihugu ageze kuri 88% by’ingengo y’imari y’uru rwego. Mu rwego rw’imibereho myiza y’abaturage amafaranga atangwa na Leta yiyongereyeho bibiri bya gatatu, kugira ngo hazibwe icyuho cyatewe no kugabanuka kw’inkunga z’abafatanyabikorwa.

Imirire n’igwingira mu bana bari munsi y’imyaka itanu byavuye kuri 33% mu 2020 bigera kuri 27% mu 2025.

Imibare y’impfu z’abana bapfaga batarageza ku myaka itanu igaragaza ko bavuye kuri 45 ku bana 1.000 bavuka ari bazima mu mwaka wa 2019/2020, bagera kuri 36 mu 2025.

Mu burezi bw’incuke, abana bitabira amashuri ugereranyije n'abagomba kuyigamo bavuye ku 24.2% mu mwaka w’amashuri wa 2021/2022 bagera kuri 50.3% mu wa 2024/2025.

Umuyobozi w'Ishami rishinzwe Ingengo y’Imari muri MINECOFIN, Jeanette Rwigamba, yavuze ko ishoramari mu baturage rikomeje kuba imwe mu nkingi z'ingenzi z'iterambere ry'u Rwanda.

Yagize ati: “Ishoramari mu baturage rikomeje kuba ku isonga muri gahunda y'iterambere ry'u Rwanda. Iyi raporo twateguye dufatanyije na UNICEF iduha amakuru ashingiye ku bimenyetso, mu gihe dutegura ingengo y'imari ya 2027/2028. Twiteguye gukorana na Minisiteri zinyuranye n'abafatanyabikorwa kugira ngo buri faranga rikoreshwe mu buryo bufitiye abana akamaro.”

Mu gihe hakomeje gutegurwa ingengo y'imari y'umwaka wa 2027/2028, raporo igaragaza ko hakwiye gushyirwa imbaraga mu kurinda amafaranga agenerwa inzego zifitiye abana akamaro, kugira ngo akomeze kugira agaciro nubwo ibiciro bikomeza kuzamuka. Ikindi ni ugukomeza gushyigikira serivisi z'ubuzima bw'ababyeyi n'abana, uburere bw'abana bato na gahunda z'imirire, cyane cyane mu gihe inkunga zituruka mu mahanga zishobora kugabanuka cyangwa guhinduka.

Mu rwego rwo gukurikiza amahame n'imihigo mpuzamahanga, UNICEF ishishikariza ibihugu kugenera uburezi amafaranga agera kuri 5% by'umusaruro mbumbe w'igihugu (GDP), cyangwa 20% by'ingengo y'imari yose.

Pierre Sage's time as Crystal Palace manager lasted just five months and 16 games

Crystal Palace have sacked manager Pierre Sage after just five months in charge, with the club bottom of the Premier League.

Former Brentford and Tottenham boss Thomas Frank is in advanced talks to take over.

Sunday's 3-1 defeat by Liverpool was Palace's fourth in succession in the Premier League.

The Eagles have won just two of their opening 10 games and also have the worst defensive record in the league, conceding 24 goals.

Palace are also 21st in the 36-team Europa League table, with one win from their four matches.

In a statement, the club said that three members of Sage's coaching staff - Jamal Alioui, Damien Della Santa and Sandy Guichard - had also left the club.

Palace added: "The club thanks Pierre and his staff for their efforts during their time in South London, and wish them well for the future.

"An update on the process of appointing a new manager will be provided in due course."

Carrick and Sage sacked in first Premier League dismissals of season - reaction

Sage is the second Premier League manager to be sacked this season, after Michael Carrick was also dismissed by Manchester United on Thursday.

The 47-year-old Frenchman was appointed on a three-year contract in June after Oliver Glasner departed at the end of last season.

He previously led Lens to a second-place finish in Ligue 1 and a first French Cup triumph in their 120-year history.

However, he has been unable to replicate Glasner's success at Palace. Glasner, now manager of Nottingham Forest , led Palace to a first FA Cup title and a Europa Conference League triumph.

Would Thomas Frank be a good fit for Crystal Palace?

Palace are winless in the league since 11 October and their losing run began with a 5-0 defeat by fierce rivals Brighton .

Sage said afterwards he felt "shame" from the defeat and admitted he did not know if he would be given time to turn Palace's fortunes around.

However, there was a degree of sympathy from some behind the scenes at Selhurst Park in the immediate aftermath of that loss.

Injuries were not kind to his plans, while the absence of forward players Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr - due to a mixture of fitness and personal issues related to both players' desire to leave the club - did not help.

However, three successive defeats followed, with Palace hitting the bar and having a goal ruled out in their loss to Liverpool at Selhurst Park.

Sage won five of his 16 games in all competitions.

Palace's next Premier League match is at Coventry on 21 November, after the international break.

Frank was sacked by Tottenham in February, after just under eight months in charge.

The former Brentford boss left Spurs 16th in the Premier League and five points above the relegation zone following an eight-match winless run in the league.

Frank or Dyche? Who should be next Palace boss?

Palace believe Frank is the man to lead the club away from relegation trouble.

Discussions are understood to have reached the closing stages amid growing hope that a deal can be struck before the start of next week when players start trickling back from international duty.

The club have explored other options: former Everton and Nottingham Forest boss Sean Dyche and Toulouse boss Jens Berthel Askou among them.

But Frank is viewed as the overwhelming favourite to replace Sage, whose failure to instil defensive robustness to the team was a key factor in his sacking.

Danish coach Frank has been out of work since being sacked by Tottenham in February and took the decision over the summer not to take a job in the close season.

In recent weeks, it is understood Fulham have taken an interest in Frank's situation amid some uncertainty over Alvaro Arbeloa's future.

But Fulham 's results have picked up in recent weeks and Palace have made their move.

KIGALI – A journey between two neighbouring countries can mean many things. It can be a business deal waiting to happen, a family reunion, a long awaited holiday or an opportunity to discover what lies beyond familiar borders.

For Rwanda and Uganda, where historical, cultural, social and economic ties have long connected their people, the ability to move between the two countries is more than a matter of transportation. It is part of what keeps their relationship alive.

On November 18, 2026, Uganda Airlines will add another link to that relationship when it launches daily scheduled flights between Entebbe and Kigali, creating new possibilities for travellers and businesses while strengthening the connection between two important East African neighbours.

The announcement was made on November 12 at Kigali Serena Hotel during a Travel Trade Engagement organised by Uganda Airlines in partnership with the Uganda High Commission in Rwanda and the Uganda Tourism Board (UTB).

Held under the theme “Strengthening Connectivity, Tourism and Business Relations Between Uganda and Rwanda,” the gathering brought together travel agents, tour operators, tourism stakeholders and industry partners to discuss how improved air connectivity could translate into opportunities for both countries.

But beyond the launch of another airline service, the discussions revealed a bigger ambition: making it easier for people, businesses and tourism industries in the region to connect.

The relationship between Rwanda and Uganda is built on connections that extend beyond their shared geography.

Families have links across both countries, businesses depend on cross-border relationships, and travellers move between them for education, tourism, professional engagements and trade.

For Michael Bulwaka, Counsellor at the Uganda High Commission in Rwanda, the introduction of Uganda Airlines flights is a welcome development that builds on these longstanding relationships.

“Uganda and Rwanda enjoy longstanding historical, cultural, social and economic relations. Our two countries share more than geographical proximity; we share deep family connections, common interests, business opportunities and a collective aspiration for prosperity,” Bulwaka said.

He emphasised that the movement of people between the two countries is essential to sustaining these relationships, noting that efficient air connectivity helps facilitate interaction and unlock opportunities in business, tourism, education and regional cooperation.

His remarks placed the new route within a broader diplomatic and economic context, where aviation serves not only as a means of transportation but also as an instrument for strengthening relationships between neighbouring countries.

Bulwaka further described Uganda Airlines as an ambassador of Uganda, connecting the country to regional and international markets while creating opportunities for trade, tourism, investment and cultural exchange.

He encouraged Rwandan travel agents to embrace the new service, noting that it would allow them to expand their businesses, develop new travel packages and serve a wider range of customers.

One of the strongest selling points of the new route is the access it provides beyond Uganda itself.

With Entebbe International Airport serving as its strategic hub, Uganda Airlines will connect passengers travelling from Rwanda to more than 18 destinations across Africa, Europe, Asia and the Middle East.

Its network includes London, Mumbai, Dubai, Lagos, Johannesburg, Nairobi, Mombasa, Kinshasa, Dar es Salaam, Kilimanjaro, Zanzibar, Lusaka, Harare, Bujumbura, Mogadishu, Juba and Accra, among other destinations.

The airline says the daily Kigali–Entebbe service will offer morning and early afternoon departures throughout the week, giving travellers additional flexibility when planning their journeys.

For someone travelling beyond Uganda, the new connection provides another gateway to a wider international network. For businesses looking to reach suppliers, clients and partners in other markets, it introduces another travel option through which those relationships can be developed.

This is where the significance of the route extends beyond the two airports. Better connectivity can make regional and international travel more accessible, allowing opportunities to move alongside the people pursuing them.

Shakila Rahim Lamar, Acting Chief Commercial Officer at Uganda Airlines, highlighted the airline’s wider expansion plans, revealing that additional aircraft are expected to join its fleet.

“More aircraft, more routes, more of Africa connected,” she said, pointing to the increased capacity, travel choices and opportunities that the expected fleet expansion will bring.

The statement reflects the airline’s ambition to grow its network and strengthen its role in connecting African destinations with one another and the rest of the world.

The entry of another airline into Kigali naturally raises questions about competition, particularly in a market already served by Rwanda’s national carrier, RwandAir.

During the engagement, Julian from Capital FM asked how Uganda Airlines intends to attract and retain customers in Rwanda and what distinct value it would bring to travellers.

In response, Shakila invited passengers to experience Uganda Airlines, explaining that its entry into Kigali was intended to improve regional connectivity and encourage greater movement across the East African Community.

She also made an important clarification: Uganda Airlines had not come to compete with RwandAir, but to complement its services and contribute to making travel across Africa better.

It was a message centred on cooperation rather than rivalry.

For travellers, the presence of additional air services can mean more choices. For the wider aviation industry, stronger connections between airlines and destinations can help create a more accessible regional travel network.

However, the real test will be how effectively the airline delivers on its promise of convenience, service and connectivity, and how well it responds to the needs of Rwandan travellers.

While the airline is introducing a new route, Rwanda’s travel and tourism industry is looking at what that connection could make possible.

Nadia Keza, Chairperson of the Rwanda Tour and Travel Association, welcomed the engagement with Uganda Airlines, the Uganda High Commission and the Uganda Tourism Board, describing the daily Kigali–Entebbe service as a significant opportunity for Rwanda’s travel trade to grow, innovate and reach new markets.

She emphasised the importance of partnerships in moving the tourism industry forward, particularly by creating opportunities for travel agents and tour operators to expand their services.

For Rwanda’s travel businesses, improved access to Uganda’s network could mean developing new travel packages, establishing partnerships with Ugandan operators and offering customers more destinations.

The opportunity is equally significant in the other direction.

Uganda, popularly known as the Pearl of Africa, is recognised for its wildlife, adventure tourism, cultural heritage, natural attractions and hospitality. From its diverse landscapes to its tourism experiences, the country offers opportunities for Rwandan travellers seeking destinations beyond their usual choices.

Likewise, Ugandan visitors can explore Rwanda’s tourism offerings, creating room for increased visitor movement in both directions.

This two way potential is important. Tourism partnerships become more valuable when they allow both countries to attract visitors, exchange experiences and benefit from each other’s destinations.

With travel agents and tour operators playing a central role in connecting customers to these experiences, the engagement provided an opportunity to build relationships that could extend well beyond the launch date.

Tourism may be one of the most visible beneficiaries of the new route, but its economic significance reaches further.

For businesses operating between Rwanda and Uganda, relationships often depend on the ability to meet partners, negotiate agreements, explore markets and maintain regular communication.

A more convenient air connection can support these activities by providing another option for business travel.

Exporters, importers, entrepreneurs and investors may benefit from improved access to potential clients, suppliers and commercial partners. Greater mobility can also encourage collaboration between companies exploring opportunities across the two markets.

These benefits are particularly relevant within the East African Community, where regional integration depends on stronger economic relationships and the movement of people, goods, services and capital.

The new route therefore adds to a wider regional ambition: making East Africa a more connected economic and tourism destination.

However, translating improved connectivity into tangible economic growth will require more than flights. Strong partnerships between tourism operators, businesses, government institutions and the aviation industry will be essential to turning the opportunity into lasting results.

The Kigali engagement was not limited to business presentations and discussions.

In a surprise moment during the event, three participants who successfully completed a challenge were awarded business-class flight tickets to destinations of their choice.

The rewards brought excitement to the gathering, giving participants an opportunity to experience the airline’s premium travel offering while adding a memorable moment to the day’s proceedings.

More importantly, the engagement gave Uganda Airlines an opportunity to interact directly with the travel trade, introduce its services and build relationships with the businesses that will play an important role in promoting the new route.

The launch of daily flights between Kigali and Entebbe marks another development in the evolving relationship between Rwanda and Uganda.

For Uganda Airlines, it represents an expansion of its regional network. For Rwanda’s travel industry, it presents an opportunity to diversify travel offerings and reach new markets. For businesses and travellers, it provides another connection between two countries whose relationships extend across generations.

Yet, the significance of the new route will ultimately be measured by what happens after the inaugural flight: the partnerships formed, the destinations discovered, the business relationships strengthened and the people who find it easier to connect.

An aircraft can bring two cities closer in hours, but the opportunities created through that connection can last much longer.

CMAT and Philomena Begley celebrating Begley receiving the Lifetime Achievement Award

Irish star CMAT made a surprise appearance at an award ceremony in Belfast on Wednesday.

The pop-star joined Philomena Begley, one of Irish country music's most loved and celebrated entertainers, on stage at the NI Music Prize.

Begley was honoured with the Lifetime Achievement Award in recognition of her 64-year career.

The country music legend performed the hit Blanket on the Ground alongside CMAT.

The NI Music Prize, an annual event celebrating music in Northern Ireland, was marking its 15th anniversary on Wednesday at Ulster Hall.

Begley's award was presented by BBC broadcaster Hugo Duncan, a longtime friend of the musician.

When Begley went on to perform Blanket on the Ground she invited CMAT, who had made a surprise appearance at the ceremony, to join her on stage.

At a concert in Belfast earlier this year, CMAT, whose real name is Ciara Mary-Alice Thompson, gave a shout-out to Begley, thanking the country legend.

Reacting to the shout-out in October, Begley told the Good Morning Ulster programme that she had never met her but had "heard so much about her".

"It's hard to beat the new generation, it's great to see them all doing well."

The pop-star joined Begley, one of Irish country music's most loved and celebrated entertainers, at the NI Music Prize

Begley added that she was "over the moon" to win the award.

Begley said she did not know what reaction to expect at the awards ceremony, but that she was "looking forward to it".

Charlotte Dryden, CEO of Oh Yeah Music Centre, who were the organisers of the NI Music Prize, said that seeing Begley and CMAT together "was something really special".

"We've had some incredible moments at the NI Music Prize over the years, but I don't think we've ever experienced an atmosphere quite like that," she said.

Philomena Begley is one of the island's most loved entertainers.

An unrivalled interpreter of country music, she has delighted audiences on stages all over the world and collaborated with country greats like Porter Wagoner and Billie Jo Spears, who first released Blanket on The Ground.

From humble beginnings in Pomeroy, County Tyrone, Begley had a simple, but happy childhood as one of eight children in a close-knit, traditional and musical family.

She always loved to sing, but had no plans of pursuing a career in music.

Begley accidentally entered the world of country music at a local dance, when she was called on stage as a dare to sing a song with the Old Cross Céilí Band.

An instant hit, she was asked to fill in as cover for someone who had taken ill in the band and suddenly became swept up in the 1960s dance-hall circuit.

In 1975, Begley was granted permission to record her own version of Blanket on the Ground from US country music star Billie Jo Spears who had released it earlier that year as the title track from the album of the same name.

Begley's version went to number five in the Irish charts and sparked some friendly rivalry between the pair.

Over the years, they became close friends, sharing many of the same hits and performing together on several occasions.

Blanket on the Ground remains one of Begley's most popular songs to this day.

Begley has captivated crowds on stages all over the world, performing everywhere from Wembley Stadium to Nashville, Tennessee.

In 1978, she was invited by Porter Wagoner, the man who introduced Dolly Parton to the world, to perform at the Grand Ole Opry, Nashville's legendary home of country music.

Here she rubbed shoulders with the stars of global country music and even received a standing ovation for her performance of Blanket on the Ground.

It was fitting recognition for her contribution to country music in Ireland and beyond.

In 2025, Begley's Blanket on the Ground becoming the unofficial anthem for the Dungannon Swifts and their journey to the Irish Cup final.

Dillon Boyd, from The Spirit of '49 Dungannon Swifts supporters club, said it all started after the Pomeroy woman's song was played on the bus radio on an away trip and "the whole place just took off".

Philomena Begley put on a special performance for Dungannon Swifts' fans and players

Speaking to BBC News NI ahead of the Irish Cup final, Ms Begley said she was "shocked, but delighted" with the response.

The Swifts went on to win the final , holding their nerve against Cliftonville to secure a 4-3 penalty shootout win after a 1-1 draw after extra time.

Country star Philomena Begley joined in the celebrations on stage

At a victory parade after the final , the Queen of Country joined players on stage for a rendition of 'Blanket on the Ground'.

There were a number of other artists honoured on Wednesday, including Joshua Burnside, who won the PPL Album of the Year award for It's Not Going to Be OK.

Belfast band Chalk, meanwhile, celebrated a double win: the group was awarded Single of the Year for Pain, as well as MCD Live Act of the Year.

Tatjana Smith won one gold and one silver medal at both the Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Olympic Games

The decision by South Africa's most decorated Olympian Tatjana Smith to switch allegiance to the Netherlands is "sad" for the nation, says Swimming South Africa CEO Zikie Molusi.

Double Olympic champion Smith, who has dual citizenship because her father is Dutch, was in tears when she announced her decision on Wednesday.

She said that the opportunity "offers greater high-performance support" and that South African athletes "deserve a system that gives them an opportunity to thrive, not just survive".

"When I received that correspondence from Tatjana we understood because she has been really generous and kind enough to articulate the rationale that informed the decision," Molusi, the acting CEO of the governing body, told eNews Channel Africa.

"A very sad decision for the country, particularly as we were preparing to take the team to Beijing for the short course World Championships in December."

Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands

Smith, formerly Schoenmaker, previously said financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, contributed to her decision to step away from the sport after the Paris 2024 Olympics.

The 29-year-old, who has won four Olympic medals, came out of retirement in September and is set to represent the Netherlands for the first time at the World Championships from 1-6 December.

Smith said representing the Netherlands would give her "the potential to build a more sustainable career".

She said the "financial and practical challenges of swimming were among the reasons my previous career became difficult to sustain".

Speaking to Radio 702, Molusi accepted that Swimming South Africa should not have withheld prize money from Smith following the 2023 World Championships.

Molusi said that was caused by conflicting sponsorship agreements but it "shouldn't have happened".

Of the 21 athletes competing for South Africa at the Worlds next month, Molusi said "probably 50% will be subsidised fully", with the rest receiving partial support.

"It's an ecosystem issue within South African sport that possibly needs to be dealt with," Molusi said.

"This comes as a result of the inadequate funding that sport federations are receiving."

Rwanda is seeking $12 billion in investment to cut greenhouse gas emissions by 53 per cent by 2035.

The commitment was announced on Thursday, November 12, by Prime Minister Dr Justin Nsengiyumva, who delivered Rwanda’s statement on behalf of President Paul Kagame at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye.

At US$12 billion, Rwanda’s climate investment requirement is equivalent to about 65 per cent of the country’s projected 2026 GDP of US$18.4 billion and more than twice its entire 2026/27 national budget of Rwf7.8 trillion (approximately US$5.2 billion).

The comparison highlights the scale of the ambition, although the US$12 billion is a multi-year requirement, not an amount Rwanda plans to spend in a single financial year.

Government says 80 per cent of the required funding is conditional on international support, making access to climate finance critical to achieving the 2035 emissions-reduction target.

The target is part of Rwanda’s third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), the country’s climate action plan under the Paris Agreement. It aims to reduce emissions by 53 per cent by 2035 compared with projected emissions under a business-as-usual scenario.

The $12 billion requirement covers the investment needed to deliver the plan. Nsengiyumva called for predictable, accessible and adequate financing for both climate adaptation and emissions reduction.

He also said developing countries needed better access to capital, arguing that viable projects were often held back by perceptions that investments in the Global South carried greater risks.

Quoting President Kagame’s recent remarks at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, he said the perception that investments in the South were riskier than those in the North was misplaced.

“Investments should be judged on their merits, not on their location,” he said.

He called on governments and the private sector to work together to make projects investable, deepen markets and mobilise financing on affordable terms without adding to unsustainable debt.

Rwanda’s climate ambitions are guided by Vision 2050 and its Green Growth and Climate Resilience Strategy, which set out a long-term pathway for economic development alongside environmental protection.

The Prime Minister also highlighted the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol, which seeks to phase down hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), powerful greenhouse gases widely used in refrigeration and air conditioning.

Rwanda recently hosted the 38th Meeting of the Parties to the Montreal Protocol, marking ten years since the adoption of the Kigali Amendment. Nsengiyumva said 175 of the protocol’s 198 parties had ratified the amendment.

If fully implemented, the amendment could prevent up to 0.5°C of global warming by 2100. Combined with improvements in energy efficiency, the benefits could reach up to one degree, he said.

He called on countries that have not yet ratified the amendment to join the agreement.

Rwanda is also preparing to assume the chairmanship of the G77 and China in 2027, a group representing developing countries in international negotiations.

Nsengiyumva said Rwanda would use the position to strengthen cooperation among developing nations and advance unresolved issues in climate negotiations, including indicators under the Global Goal on Adaptation that relate to financial needs and the provision of climate finance.

He said COP31 should be judged not only by the commitments made but by the practical action delivered.

Sir Elton has long been a supporter of the King's Trust charity

King Charles III has appeared on Sir Elton John's radio show in an episode set to coincide with the monarch's 78th birthday.

During the Rocket Hour show, the King said the pop star had become "a national treasure after all these years", to which the singer joked: "I'll be on the Antiques Roadshow."

The pair discussed some of their favourite musical performances, as well as the role music has played in the King's charity, the King's Trust. The show was recorded in secret last month and will air this Saturday.

Sir Elton has long been a supporter of the trust, most recently donating a pair of his rose-tinted glasses to its 50th anniversary auction this year.

In a trailer for the upcoming episode, the King and Sir Elton are seen laughing together as they chat.

In a voiceover, the singer said he was "excited to hear what he's got to say about music, about the King's Trust and memories that we both share".

The King's Trust - previously known as The Prince's Trust - was established by Charles in 1976 to help young people from disadvantaged backgrounds overcome challenging situations, become employed or launch their own businesses.

During the radio episode, the King called it "an opportunity too good to resist" when he was asked to showcase music from the "talented performers who have so generously supported us over the years, together with some of the newer artists the trust has helped to launch".

The full list of their chosen tracks is under wraps until the episode airs but Skye Newman's Hairdresser, Raye's Joy and Muse's rendition of Feeling Good are said to be among them.

The pair will reminisce about some of the most memorable performances for the trust, from the Wembley Arena rock galas of the 1980s - which Sir Elton participated in - to charity shows at the Royal Albert Hall and pop concerts in Hyde Park.

The episode was recorded at Apple Music Studios - which hosts the show - in Battersea Power Station when the King and Sir Elton visited for the launch of the Apple x King's Trust Creative Labs.

The mentorship programme aims to help young people explore careers in creative industries.

More than 1,600 cases involving civil society organisations in Rwanda have been recorded as not meeting legal or regulatory requirements, according to a report by the Rwanda Governance Board (RGB) to Parliament.

The figures cover local and international non-governmental organisations (NGOs), foundations and faith-based organisations. They include organisations that failed to meet requirements for registration, legal personality, operational certificates and compliance with government directives.

A closer breakdown of the figures, however, shows that 1,453 applications were classified as not meeting requirements. The broader figure of 1,612 also includes 159 local NGOs that did not apply for the compliance certificate required under the new law.

Legal requirements differ across civil society organisations. Local NGOs must provide recognised leadership, notarised statutes, district collaboration letters, annual financial and activity reports, and action plans.

International NGOs must demonstrate authorisation in their countries of origin, donor funding and approval to operate in Rwanda.

Foundations must show their initial assets, objectives and governance structures.

Faith-based organisations face additional requirements covering worship premises, leaders’ qualifications, financial audits, donor identification and safeguards against money laundering and terrorist financing. They must also provide 1,000 supporting members when seeking a district collaboration letter. This is not a universal membership requirement for all existing churches.

Local NGOs account for the largest share of the cases. A total of 536 did not meet the requirements for a compliance certificate, while 210 failed to meet requirements for legal personality. Another 159 did not apply to harmonise their operations with the law.

Together, these cases bring the number involving local NGOs to 905 under the broader calculation.

Among international NGOs, 27 did not meet requirements for new operational certificates, two failed to meet requirements for legal personality, and 25 did not meet the conditions for renewal of their operational certificates. The total is 54.

Foundations recorded 52 cases in which requirements for legal personality were not met.

Faith-based organisations accounted for 601 cases. Five did not meet requirements for legal personality, while 596 did not comply with additional guidelines issued by RGB on March 7, 2025.

The report also records organisations that met the requirements and received approvals. These include 179 local NGOs granted compliance certificates and 174 granted legal personality.

Among international NGOs, 15 received new operational certificates, eight were granted legal personality and 82 received extensions of their operational registration.

For foundations, 33 were granted legal personality. In the faith-based sector, four received legal personality, while the report’s summary records six organisations as having met the additional guidelines.

Using these figures, RGB recorded 501 approvals across the different processes. The report does not establish that these represent 501 distinct organisations, since one organisation may have applied for more than one approval.

The figures also leave 260 local NGO compliance applications under review. These have not been counted among those that failed to meet requirements.

The distinction is important because the figures do not necessarily mean that all the organisations listed have been closed. Failure to meet a particular requirement, loss of legal personality, and suspension or closure of operations are different regulatory outcomes.

Rwanda’s Law No. 058/2024 governing NGOs introduced a unified legal framework for civil society organisations. It requires organisations to meet registration and compliance conditions set by RGB.

The report’s figures therefore provide a picture of the scale of compliance work across the sector, but do not, on their own, establish how many organisations have permanently ceased operations or been formally shut down.

Former BBC Radio 1 and Capital Xtra DJ Tim Westwood has denied two more sexual offences during a court hearing.

His latest pleas of not guilty mean he now denies a total of 17 charges concerning allegations by nine women between 1983 and 2016.

The 69-year-old pleaded not guilty to indecently assaulting a teenage girl aged 16 or 17 in Hammersmith and Fulham, west London, in 1991 at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday.

At the same hearing, Westwood also denied sexually assaulting an 18-year-old woman in Wandsworth, south London, in May 2004.

Westwood, of Fitzrovia, in London's West End, was charged in October last year with offences against seven women, which he also denies.

He is accused of four indecent assaults in the 1980s in London, as well as three indecent assaults while at the BBC in the 1990s.

The defendant is also alleged to have raped a woman in a hotel in 1996.

Westwood is further accused of two indecent assaults and one count of rape from the early 2000s at a London address, and two counts of rape at a London address in the 2010s.

He is also alleged to have committed a sexual assault at a nightclub in Stroud, Gloucestershire, in 2010 and at a London music festival in 2016.

Westwood has been granted conditional bail and is due to face a seven-week trial at Southwark Crown Court starting on 27 January.

A snail-eating horned frog discovered in India has been named Jingophrys tanogogo

Scientists have discovered five new species of tiny horned frogs in India's eastern Himalayas, more than doubling the number of known species in the group.

A team of scientists from University of Delhi and Harvard University made the discoveries after five years of fieldwork, identifying the frogs as members of the Jingophrys group.

Among them is Jingophrys tanogogo - or the snail-eating horned frog - the first frog known in India to feed on snails and the first member of its family recorded with such a diet.

The research suggest the Himalayas have played a much larger role in frog evolution than previously thought and highlight the region as an overlooked hotspot for biodiversity.

Some discoveries, such as the Jingophrys taniitatii, were named to honour the local tribes that helped the researchers

Jingophrys hrdy or the Hrdy's horned frog is among the miniature frogs discovered in India's Arunachal Pradesh state

The Himalayas, stretching from tropical forests to alpine meadows, are among the world's richest biodiversity regions.

Despite drawing interest from scientists and researchers, many parts here have not been fully explored.

The state of Arunachal Pradesh particularly has emerged as one of its least-studied regions.

Dr Sonali Garg, who led the study at Harvard University's Museum of Comparative Zoology, said the research highlights how significant evolutionary changes can go unnoticed in little-studied species.

The study - called two-fold hidden diversity of diminutive horned frogs (Megophryinae: Jingophrys) - was conducted by Garg along with her colleague James Hanken and Delhi University's SD Biju, Tage Tajo and Radhakrishna Upadhyaya K.

It was published on 11 November in the Royal Society Open Science journal.

Researchers say they will have to carry out more studies to better understand the biology of the new species, including Jingophrys siangensis ( Siang horned frog)

"Some of the new species are extremely secretive and found in remote forests only during a short breeding season," says Biju.

Researchers say further studies will have to done to better understand their biology and conservation needs.

DNA analysis showed the horned frogs rapidly diversified into multiple species in the eastern Himalayas as the mountain range rose and the Asian monsoon took shape over millions of years, helping drive the evolution of the region's plants and wildlife.

The researchers said in a statement that local tribes gave them essential field support and knowledge that helped make the discoveries possible. Some of the species were named after these communities.

The Tanii horned frog (Jingophrys taniitatii), for instance, is named by combining the name of the Tanii tribe in the region with the word 'tatti' - frog in the local Apatani language.

The new species have been named Jingophrys taniitatii (Tanii horned frog), Jingophrys tanogogo (snail-eating horned frog), Jingophrys siangensis (Siang horned frog), Jingophrys hrdy (Hrdy's horned frog) and Jingophrys wularsoni (Wu-Larson's horned frog).

PM Andy Burnham was the only G7 leader to go to COP31

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has warned that the consensus on both science and climate change has "gone".

Addressing other world leaders and delegates at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey, he said that despite this, the UK was ready to begin a "new era of British leadership" on the climate change issue.

But environmental campaigners at the summit said the PM had to back up his warm words with stronger actions.

In recent months, the UK government has announced policies which critics say have weakened its green credentials, such as reducing support for heat pumps, approving the Jackdaw gas field and doubling down on support for Heathrow Airport's expansion.

Burnham opened his speech on Thursday by talking about the heat experienced in the UK this past summer.

He said "it was not normal" - in fact it was the hottest on record, made 130 times more likely because of climate change, according to the Met Office .

Hundreds of schools were closed, cereal harvests were down 11%, and ambulance services were inundated with calls beyond levels seen during the Covid-19 pandemic.

As a result of the threat to people's health and homes, the PM said he was creating the UK, and the world's, first climate security envoy, Dame Madeleine Alessandri.

Alessandri, the former head of the Joint Intelligence Committee, said: "Climate change and nature loss are increasingly shaping the security environment in which the UK operates."

As a result this was "placing additional pressure on resources, economies and communities around the world", she added.

This will be seen as a strong indication of the focus of the UK's priorities when it takes up the G20 presidency next year.

The current president is the US, which has been a notable absentee from the COP process over the last two years since President Trump withdrew the country from the most important global climate treaty - the Paris Climate Agreement.

Professor Lord Nicholas Stern, who identified 20 years ago that climate change could cost the global economy up to 20% of GDP if left unchecked, praised the PM's words.

"The Prime Minister was right to identify climate change as a threat to security around the world, and the importance of investments in clean electricity generation as the best way of protecting households and businesses from the high prices and volatile markets for fossil fuels," he said.

Homes in the West Midlands were destroyed after record wildfires this summer in the UK

On tackling the causes of climate change, Burnham said his government remained committed to meeting the country's target of net zero by 2050 whilst also getting bills down.

He said key to this was cutting our "dependence on fossil fuels" and increasing electrification - the amount of our energy needs met from renewable electricity.

The main driver of rising global temperatures has been the increasing concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, largely caused by burning fossil fuels.

Turkey, the co-hosts of COP31, wants a key outcomes of this year's summit to be a commitment by countries to meet 35% of their energy supply from electricity by 2035. Currently, it is around a fifth.

But Burnham has been accused of having double standards.

"The Prime Minister simply cannot call for clean power across the world while saying yes to more fossil fuels in the UK," said Beth John, climate adviser at Oxfam.

Last month, the government approved the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea on the grounds that it provided energy security.

And in the budget last month Chancellor John Healey announced a funding cut to the Warm Homes Plan, which provides grants and loans to support the installation of heat pumps.

Whilst this week there has been media speculation that the government is considering watering down electric car sales targets, although the government insists no decision has been made.

Successfully switching petrol and diesel cars to EVs and moving from gas boilers to electric-powered heat pumps are key ways to achieve the 35% electrification target , external .

The BBC's climate editor, Justin Rowlatt, investigates the impact of the changing climate on our weather.

Watch on BBC iPlayer or on BBC One (BBC Two in Northern Ireland) at 20:00 on Monday 9 November.

Although there was no royal presence this year, King Charles III sent a message ahead of Burnham's speech.

"As the world gathers for Cop31, I can only hope that this same spirit of partnership and common purpose can help inspire the collective action that our planet – and future generations – so urgently need.

"Our children and grandchildren will not judge us by the promises we made, but by what we chose to do."

Burnham was the only G7 leader to speak at this year's conference in a sign of faltering support for the COP process - something he acknowledged in his speech.

In an almost word for word copy of Sir Keir Starmer's address last year he said: "The consensus we once enjoyed on science and climate has gone, and the reality is now the world will reach 1.5 degrees."

Other leaders expected to speak on Thursday include many island states like Tonga, Tuvalu and the Solomon Islands.

For these nations, the impact of climate change is already at their front door. With most of their land just metres above sea level, rising water levels have caused many to abandon their homes in recent years.

Last year, Australia - the co-host of the COP31 summit - opened up the world's first climate visa for Tuvalu citizens wanting to evacuate.

The first intake was massively oversubscribed, with more than a third of the population entering the ballot.

As glaciers continue to melt and oceans expand, average sea levels are expected to keep climbing and potentially accelerate. The World Meteorological Organisation said on the opening day of this conference the global mean sea level was at its highest level since records began.

“President Kagame and First Lady Jeannette Kagame have arrived in Phnom Penh for a State Visit to the Kingdom of Cambodia, ahead of the 20th Francophonie Summit,” the Rwandan Presidency said earlier Thursday.

President Kagame will meet the country’s top leaders and witness the signing of several bilateral cooperation agreements ahead of the 20th Francophonie Summit.

During his visit, Kagame will be granted a royal audience with King Sihamoni at the Royal Palace and hold separate meetings with Senate President Hun Sen, National Assembly President Khuon Sudary and Mr Hun Manet.

Those privy with information of this visit in Cambodia told Taarifa Investigative Desk discussions between the two leaders will focus on strengthening bilateral relations and expanding cooperation between their countries.

*Several agreements and cooperation documents covering trade, investment, aviation and tourism are expected to be signed, paving the way for closer economic and business ties between the two countries,” according to a statement issued by the Cambodia Foreign Affairs ministry.

MN202611_a0eidbb5gd.t:
PHNOM PENH – President Paul Kagame is in Cambodia for his first state visit to the Southeast Asian country, where he is expected to hold talks with the country’s top leaders and sign agreements aimed at expanding trade, investment, aviation and tourism cooperation.

Kagame is accompanied by First Lady Jeannette Kagame and a high-level delegation.

The visit, at the invitation of King Norodom Sihamoni, comes ahead of the 20th Summit of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF), which Cambodia will host in Phnom Penh from November 14 to 16.

The visit is also a milestone in relations between the two countries, which established diplomatic ties in 2005.

Despite the geographical distance, both governments have been working to expand cooperation in areas of shared interest.

During his stay, Kagame is scheduled to meet King Norodom Sihamoni at the Royal Palace. He will also hold separate meetings with Senate President Hun Sen, National Assembly President Khuon Sudary and Prime Minister Hun Manet.

The discussions are expected to focus on strengthening political relations and expanding economic cooperation. Several agreements and cooperation documents are expected to be signed, covering trade, investment, aviation and tourism.

The Cambodian government says the agreements are intended to strengthen business ties and create new opportunities for cooperation. Details of the individual agreements have not yet been announced.

The visit builds on agreements signed during Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn’s visit to Kigali in November 2025.

The two countries signed a memorandum of understanding establishing regular consultations between their foreign ministries. They also signed an agreement exempting holders of diplomatic and official passports from visa requirements.

The agreements were intended to create a framework for more regular diplomatic engagement and easier official travel between the two countries.

Cooperation has also been discussed in financial services and digital payments, areas that could support trade and tourism as the relationship develops.

After the state visit, Kagame will attend the 20th Summit of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF), taking place in Phnom Penh from November 15 to 16, following ministerial meetings on November 14.

Cambodia is hosting the summit for the first time. It will bring together leaders and representatives of French-speaking countries under the theme, “Reinvest in Peace for Shared Prosperity and Lasting Stability.” More than 20 heads of state and government are expected to attend.

One of the main issues on the agenda is the election of the OIF Secretary-General for the 2027–2030 term.

Rwanda’s Louise Mushikiwabo, who has led the organisation since 2018, is seeking a third term. She faces three challengers: Juliana Amato Lumumba of the Democratic Republic of Congo, former Mauritanian minister Coumba Bâ and former Romanian Prime Minister Dacian Cioloș.

The election is scheduled for November 16 and is expected to attract considerable diplomatic attention, particularly because Rwanda and the DRC are backing rival candidates.

Kagame’s presence at the summit therefore carries significance beyond Rwanda’s participation in the Francophonie.

It comes at a time when the organisation is preparing to choose its next leader and when the competing candidacies have become part of wider diplomatic discussions.

For Rwanda, the Cambodia visit offers two opportunities: to build stronger ties with a country in Southeast Asia and to engage with fellow Francophone leaders on the organisation’s future.

Arm's boss Rene Haas (L), Nvidia's Colette Kress (C) and Chris Malachowsky (R) have been named as possible successors

Nvidia is now facing a scenario few would have considered until very recently - a future without Jensen Huang.

The influential co-founder of the AI chip-making giant resigned on Thursday over reports of extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is in charge, for now, as the tech giant faces one of its biggest challenges - finding the right person to permanently lead the business that Huang helped create more than three decades ago and turned into one of the world's most valuable companies.

We take a look at which candidates have emerged as potential successors.

Colette Kress is chief financial officer at Nvidia

Colette Kress has been an industry veteran for more than 30 years, having previously held high positions at tech firms like Cisco and Microsoft.

Kress, who also serves as Nvidia's executive vice-president, has seen the firm's transformation from making chips for video games in the early 1990s to becoming an AI semiconductor powerhouse.

She has "fronted every earnings call" alongside Huang and is a "familiar and trusted voice for the market at a time when it badly needs one," said Josh Gilbert, an analyst at investment firm eToro.

But doing the job permanently could be a different story, said Gilbert, as the firm, known for its edge in technology, could want an engineer in the chair.

Chris Malachowsky is one of Nvidia's three co-founders

Another option is Chris Malachowsky, who founded Nvidia alongside Huang and Curtis Priem, and is the only executive that shares the same level of seniority.

Malachowsky has played a key part in developing the company's computing technology.

Ian Buck, who oversees Nvidia's high-performance computing business, has also emerged as a potential candidate if the company is keen to put an engineer in the top job.

Buck was among the early pioneers who helped popularise the use of graphic processors beyond gaming applications.

"He could protect Nvidia's technological edge, but his ability to manage the wider commercial relationships and geopolitical challenges would face scrutiny," said Charu Chanana, investment strategist at investment bank Saxo.

Today, Nvidia's leading processors are widely regarded as the gold standard for AI development.

Huang's children also work at Nvidia in executive positions but are relatively young and inexperienced.

Nvidia is likely to favour an internal appointment initially but could look externally for a more permanent replacement, said Jun Bei Liu, founder and lead portfolio manager at Ten Cap.

Several names of tech entrepreneurs outside of Nvidia have been floated by experts.

US President Donald Trump suggested Apple's former chief executive, Tim Cook, as a good replacement.

"NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!" he wrote on Truth Social.

Liu said Cook could be a possible choice as someone familiar with managing global supply chains, though she questioned whether he would be willing to leave the iPhone maker, where he is the chair.

Apple's Tim Cook (R) with Jensen Huang (L) and his wife Lori Huang at the White House

Liu and Chanana also suggested Rene Haas, chief executive of Arm Holdings, the UK chip designer.

Nvidia's processors are made with the help of chipmakers around the world, including Taiwan's TSMC and South Korea's SK Hynix and Samsung.

Haas is familiar with leading a publicly-listed company and would bring semiconductor experience, though Nvidia's business model is considerably different from Arm's, said Chanana.

"The challenge is finding someone who can combine Jensen's technical understanding, strategic vision and relationships across the global technology industry," Liu said.

Ten Cap's Liu had believed it was just a matter of time before Huang would step down as Nvidia's chief executive.

"The issue is no longer simply about personal conduct," she said. "It is about corporate governance, national security concerns and maintaining confidence in the leadership of one of the world's most strategically important companies."

Several major investment firms have downgraded their forecasts for the chip giant - a rare shift given investors' longstanding optimism about the company.

An early indication came as markets opened in New York shortly after Huang's resignation was announced.

Nvidia shares opened down more than 13%, wiping more than half a trillion dollars off the firm's share market value.

Jensen Huang's departure leaves a void in the influential AI giant

Stacy Rasgon, senior analyst in US semiconductors at Bernstein Research, wrote in a note to investors that "our gut tells us we probably haven't fully probed the depths of what might be found here".

Rasgon halved Bernstein's share price target for Nvidia and said: "We've had enough and prefer to watch from the sidelines."

Ray Wang, chief executive of Constellation Research, said the crisis isn't so much an issue for the wider AI industry but rather one for Nvidia itself which has to consider if the person it appoints as its chief executive has the same appeal as Huang.

"That's really what the issue is, because a lot of these partnerships and investments have been made because of the trust with with Jensen," he said.

Six PL games that defined Carrick's Man Utd tenure

It was just after 6pm on Sunday, 8 November when the message landed. Manchester United were 4-2 down to Aston Villa, and Old Trafford was resigned to defeat.

The plea came from someone who knows Michael Carrick well, has worked with him and understands at first hand the pressures of life in the United goldfish bowl.

As it turned out, the predicted ending did not come to pass.

United scored twice in stoppage time to salvage a 4-4 draw. Carrick celebrated Patrick Dorgu's equaliser by raising an arm in the air. After that, he walked round the pitch on what has turned out to be a final lap of appreciation.

As the United supporters sang his name, Carrick placed himself in the middle of his players to ensure the fans did not turn on them in the way they had done after the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth two weeks before.

It was a decision that summed up the 45-year-old - supporting the collective, rather than looking after himself.

That obvious desire to do the best for his club and his players - and his storied past - explains why Carrick's song continued to be bellowed from the stands when just about everyone else involved at United was attracting fury and derision.

To get this far is longer than many envisaged. It seemed there was no way Carrick could survive the Bournemouth debacle.

United took 44 hours to communicate to the wider world they were sticking with him then, though it is understood Carrick was told the day before.

Since then, it has been chaos. United have won one, drawn one and lost one.

Outstanding in the opening 45 minutes at Chelsea, they conceded at the start of the second half before defender Lisandro Martinez was sent off for two bookings in the space of five minutes. They lost 2-0.

Awful and two goals down inside 17 minutes against Roma in the Champions League, they roared back with the kind of thrilling comeback Carrick was part of so often during Sir Alex Ferguson's days to win 3-2.

Then, Villa. Two goals down in four minutes thanks to calamitous goalkeeping, they clawed back to level before half-time. More abysmal defending left United with another mountain to climb - but they emerged from the carnage with a point.

Try picking the bones out of that. Had Carrick's stock increased, or had it merely proven he was not the right man the job? United decided it was the latter.

United came from two goals down twice to snatch a draw against Villa

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox celebrated Dorgu's stoppage-time equaliser against Villa in the directors' box. But they had a slightly detached perspective.

Within days they were flying to Monaco to tell minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe change was required.

For the third season in a row, United are replacing the man in charge of the team mid-season.

Unlike with Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, this decision is not a surprise. Not because of what is happening now, but because what is happening now is so at odds with what happened last season.

After 12 wins in 17 games under Carrick and a return to the Champions League, the mood in pre-season was overwhelmingly positive.

There were no signs of splits, young players including JJ Gabriel were part of the group, and senior staff spoke optimistically about the potential of Bruno Fernandes' proposed partnership with Youri Tielemans.

Recruitment was clearly an issue, but more of that later.

Man Utd fan wants to know why Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada haven't been sacked

Looking back, the 48 hours before United's season-opening match at Hull were pivotal.

With Benjamin Sesko still trying to ease his way back from the shin issue that ended his previous campaign early, Amad Diallo suffered an ankle injury that would rule him out for seven weeks. It meant Carrick was deprived of his first-choice striking alternative, with Bryan Mbeumo having to play on the right of the attack.

Carrick instead turned to Matheus Cunha, whose preference for dropping deep took him into the spaces captain Fernandes likes to occupy.

It neutralised United's attack on a day they seemed ill-prepared to meet the physical challenge of an opponent motivated by their long-awaited Premier League return.

In his role as interviewer for Nordic broadcaster Viaplay, former Norway and Middlesbrough striker Jan Aage Fjortoft claimed United had lacked passion - something Carrick dismissed as "ridiculous".

"It's one game," Carrick told the media afterwards.

The following week, United were losing to Ipswich - another newly promoted side. Only a slip from Marcelino Nunez inside his own half allowed Cunha to tee up Fernandes for an undeserved equaliser. Fernandes, who had just been crowned PFA Player of the Year for 2025-26, went on to complete a hat-trick in a 5-2 win.

United have not won in the Premier League since.

After that came a trip to Everton. Twice United led, the second time when Sesko struck two minutes from time after coming on as a substitute. Deep into stoppage time, Ainsley Maitland-Niles drove home from long range to deny the visitors.

Asked how confident he was in his side's ability to react to a disappointing start to the season, Carrick snapped back: "It's not been that bad."

Manchester United's 4-1 defeat by Como was one of their worst European results

Time and again, United's fitness was called into question. They struggled badly against a Manchester City side reduced to 10 men in the first half before City benefited from an Erling Haaland goal that referees' chief Howard Webb later admitted should not have stood.

Carrick's complaints after the match were justified - but they masked a poor performance from his team.

After taking a 2-0 lead inside 10 minutes against Brighton in the EFL Cup, United were outplayed and beaten, thanks to two goals in four second-half minutes.

Carrick's coaching staff - lauded months earlier - could not find an answer.

The head coach said Cunha's injury-time equaliser against a Fulham side who started the game bottom was a positive to build on. But immediately after the international break, United were held to another draw - conceding in injury time to an out-of-form and 10-man Tottenham.

The familiar downward spiral was getting out of control.

Martinez was at fault for Spurs' leveller, which made his post-match outburst after the 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid more amazing.

The Argentina defender criticised United's summer recruitment and placed the blame at the door of "the technical director" - Wilcox.

By the time of Martinez's outburst, Sesko and left-back Luke Shaw were injured. Marcus Rashford has not played since. The rotation at left-back eventually led to Carrick starting five different players in that role.

After conceding in the opening minute against Atletico, Como scored inside the first two in a 4-1 win. Fernandes came out afterwards and criticised Carrick's tactics.

He was dropped for the Bournemouth game, but returned as captain at Chelsea.

Sesko has started two games and scored two goals this season

There is no doubt Carrick made mistakes. The Hull game - a performance that set the tone for the season so far - was inexplicable.

But it is also fair to wonder how much he was let down by the recruitment side.

A source close to one player questioned why so much attention was focused on midfield, when the inevitable consequence was Fernandes being shifted away from the central position he excelled in over the second half of last season.

Casemiro's exit necessitated a big-money replacement but, after heading down one-way streets in the pursuit of Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest and Mateus Fernandes from West Ham, it was 25 August before the £70m deal to sign Carlos Baleba from Brighton was completed.

A pre-existing ankle injury meant Baleba did not make his debut until 10 October. After starting only five games, he is now out for an extended period with a hamstring problem.

Tielemans arrived from Aston Villa for £35m and Andrey Santos signed from Chelsea in a deal that could eventually cost £50m. The former scored his first goal in the Villa thriller. Santos, though, was left on the bench. He has started four league games.

Meanwhile, obvious issues in Carrick's squad were left unaddressed.

Shaw started every Premier League game last season, but that was an outlier in an otherwise injury-hit career. Clear competition was needed in that area. Instead, United backed off, thinking they might be able to sign Lewis Hall from Newcastle next summer.

United's back four for the first home game of the season was the same as it was for the first home game under Ten Hag in 2022. They have conceded 30 goals so far this term - the most of any team in Europe's top five leagues, apart from Lens.

Up front, Sesko finished last season injured and had only made two substitute appearances when the transfer window closed. Carrick subsequently admitted he would be out for a "long time" - thought to be at least January.

United's players were booed down the tunnel by their own fans after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth

Carrick was asked about the possibility of further signings following the arrivals of Tielemans and Santos during the club's pre-season training camp on 13 August.

"We want more, we need more," was the response.

For someone so calm and considered, it was a strong demand for action to those above. Well-placed sources say it was obvious to Carrick where the holes in his squad were and he was expecting more than a single new signing from that point.

A couple of weeks before Carrick spoke, another club source told BBC Sport that United should be judged when the transfer window closed.

From this position, that judgement would have to be negative.

However, other United sources defend the recruitment strategy, claiming it easy to be wise after the event and at the end of last season, Kobbie Mainoo was their only orthodox midfield option.

It is also argued the United squad is capable of finishing in the Champions League places.

More than a quarter of the way into the season, they are some way off that target.

Carrick has paid the price - lasting less than six months into the two-year contract he signed in May.

Mauricio Pochettino will be his replacement. Berrada and Wilcox will hope his appointment brings calm after another period of chaos.

Kyryll, afise imyaka 12, avuga icongereza neza cane, ururimi yize mu kiringo c'imyaka ibiri yamaze muri Reta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika. Aravuga ata guca ku ruhande ingaruka iri cika ry'umuyagankuba rigira ku buzima bwabo.

Ati: "Nta muco, nta mazi, nta buryo bwo gushusha, nta muyagankuba. Nta n'ukuryoherwa n'ubuzima bikibaho".

Abandanya ati: "Ibintu vyose vyaduhimbara ntibikibaho. Dufise imikino myinshi ngaha y'amakarata, n'ibindi bikoresho bijanye. Aho tubibika haruzuye, ariko turamaze kuyikina nk'incuro ibihumbi amajana, kubera umuyagankuba uba wagiye."

Imiryango myinshi usanga iri mu kizime, mu gihe ibice vyose vy'ibisagara umuyagankuba uguma ucika.

Daryna agira ati: «Uravye hanze, rimwe rimwe nta na kimwe ubona. Uba uri mu gisagara kinini ariko ntubona na kimwe kubera umwijima."

Igisagara ca Kyiv ni co cakozweko cane n'ivyo bitero. N'amatereni canke imodoka zunguruza ingenzi mu gisagara zikoresheje umuyagankuba, kenshi zirahagarara. Mu gihugu cose, mu ndwi ziheruka, Abanya Ukraine ibihumbi amajana baramaze igihe ata muyagankuba bafise.

Mu rugendo twagiriye kuri kimwe mu bigo ntanganguvu binini cane muri Ukraine, twariboneye igituma bigenda uko. Ico kigo casa nk'aho casenyutse cose, kubera ibitero cari giherutse kugabwako hakoreshejwe misire yo mu bwoko bwa 'balistique'. Cari co gitero gikomeye kandi casambuye vyinshi kuruta ibindi vyose mu vyo Uburusiya bumaze kugaba ku bibanza vy'inguvu vya Ukraine.

Ico kigo kinini cane gitanga umuyagankuba - twasabwe kutakivuga izina ku mvo z'umutekano - carasambutse ku buryo casigaye ari nk'ikirundo c'ivyuma vyononekaye, imiringoti y'amazi nayo iravunagurika iyindi iragondama. Imashini zaco zitanga umuyagankuba zarafuriwe n'ibibomoke, bituma gihagarika burundu ibikorwa vyaco.

"Cari igitero kidasanzwe. Ntitwari bwigere tubona igisa naco. Ibisenge vy'inyubakwa vyari bisanzwe vyarakorotse, ariko iki gitero cari giteye ubwoba mu buryo budasanzwe", ni ko Volodymyr Kovalenko, umwe mu bakozi yari muri ico kibanza umusi haba igitero.

Kovalenko, yakurikiye amakanda y'abavyeyi biwe na we agatangura gukorera muri ico kigo, akaba amaze imyaka 25 ahakora, avuga ko iyo abonye ivyahononekariye bimubabaza cane. Gusa, yizigiye ko bishobora gusanurwa.

Hari iyindi ngorane. Ibikorwa vyo gusanura ico kigo gihambaye cane biguma bidindizwa n'imburi zigabisha ko hagira habe ibindi bitero ziba buri minota 15 canke 30. Mu masaha ane twahamaze, izo mburi zatanzwe incuro indwi. Igihe cose hamenyeshejwe ko hari 'drones' canke misire ziriko ziraza, abakozi baca bahagarika akazi bakihutira kurondera aho bikinga. Ariko mu gihe twari tuhari, izo 'drones' zararashwe izindi zibandanya zerekeza mu bundi burere.

Vadym Bobyr, arongoye ibikorwa vyo gusanura agira ati: "Biragoye cane. Uba witeguriye gukora igikorwa kanaka, maze bukwi na bukwi ukumva imburi ziravuze, ugaca wihutira kuva aho uri ukaja kwikinga."

Uyu mugabo w'imyaka 39, amaze hafi igice c'ubuzima bwiwe akorera muri ico kigo, urabona ko yaherewe iyo ariko arihweza ibisigarira vy'inyubakwa zasambutse.

Avuga ati: "Biratuntuza umutima, kuko ibi vyose twari twaramaze kubisanura, uruganda rukongera gukora. None ubu vyasubiriye guterwa. Biratubabaza, ariko turabandanya dukora no kurangura ibikorwa dutegerezwa gukora.»

Tukiriko turayaga, haciye hatangwa iyindi mburi ivuga ko hari misire iriko iraza.

Abakozi baca biruka bashwiragira ata wujanye n'uwundi baciye mu nzira nyinshi ziri hagati y'inyubakwa no mu miyoboro itandukanye, ariko ntibashobora gushika mu kibanza co kwikingamwo. Baca bahitamwo kwinyegeza inyuma y'uruhome rumwe mu zikomeye cane kuri ico kigo. Iyo misire yahavuye itangirwa n'ubuhinga bwo kwikingira ibitero vyo mu kirere iranasamburwa. Yasamburiwe nko ku birometero bitatu uvuye aho.

Abakozi bo mu gisata c'amasoko ntanganguvu bari mu kaga gakomeye cane. Kuva muri Myandagaro (8), ibitero ku bigo ntanganguvu biba hafi imisi yose, bigahitana abantu benshi, buri ndwi. Kandi uko imisi igenda, ni ko akaga karushiriza kwiyongera.

Ku ruhande rw'ico kigo, iyo akaga kagabanutse, umurwi w'abakozi uca usubira mu gikorwa co gusubizaho imihora y'umuyagankuba. Ariko, biragoye ko ico kigo kizosubira kumera neza ku buryo cotanga umuyagankuba mu banyagihugu, imbere y'uko igihe c'imbeho kirangira.

Perezida wa Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelensky, avuga ko igihugu kigifise ubushobozi buhagije bwo gutanga umuyagankuba ukenewe. Avuga ko ingorane ari ukuntu uwo muyagankuba ushobora gushikanwa mu mazu no mu bijanye n'ubucuruzi, mu gihe imihora myinshi hamwe n'ibibanza ntanganguvu vyagabweko ibitero.

Uburusiya buriko bukoresha 'drones' zitwa «waiter drones», zishobora kumata ku biti vy'umuyagankuba canke ku ntsinga, zikamara igihe ata n'umwe arazibona gushika aho Uburusiya bufashe ingingo yo kuzituritsa.

Several leaders from the Francophonie bloc have begun jetting in Cambodia ahead of the 20th Francophonie Summit.

The Capital of Cambodia, Phnom Penh is ready to host the Summit on November 14 to 16, 2026.

The Summit is themed; “Reinvesting in peace for shared prosperity and lasting stability”.

Leaders are expected to adopt a Phnom Penh Declaration on the Summit’s peace theme and elect the secretary-general for the 2027–2030 term.

Alongside the main event, the FrancoTech trade fair at Koh Pich, a France-Cambodia Business Forum and a five-day Francophonie Village will bring together business leaders, artists and young people.

Why take La Francophonie Summit to Cambodia?

Cambodia has a long history with the Francophonie.

The late King Father Norodom Sihanouk was among the founding figures of the multilateral Francophonie in 1970, and Cambodia became a full member in 1993.

This is the first time the Kingdom is hosting the Summit and only the second time it is held in Asia, following Hanoi in 1997.

Hosting the event also gives Cambodia the organisation’s rotating chairmanship until the 21st Summit in 2028.

The Summit is an opportunity for Cambodia to demonstrate what it can contribute to the Francophonie and to turn its presidency into a meaningful contribution to world peace and development while advancing its foreign policy objectives of promoting peaceful settlement of disputes, peaceful co-existence, rules-based international order, and open and inclusive multilateralism.
